Proposed Revisions to the LS Power Grid California, LLC Transmission Owner 
Tariff to Provide for Large Load Interconnection and Cost Recovery 
Dear Secretary Reese: 
Pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)1 and Part 35 of the Federal Energy 
Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC” or “Commission”) regulations,2 and in response to the 
Commission’s order instituting the show cause proceeding in California Independent System 
Operator Corp.,3 LS Power Grid California, LLC (“LS Power Grid”) submits revisions to its 
Transmission Owner Tariff (“TO Tariff”) to establish a framework for the interconnection of Large 
Loads4 and for the recovery of the costs of transmission upgrades driven by Large Loads. The 
revisions include (1) adding a new Section 10A and a new Appendix VI (Large Load 
Interconnection Procedures (“LLIP”)) to establish an interconnection process for Eligible 
Customers for Large Load (“ECLLs”); (2) corresponding revisions to the TO Tariff; and (3) adding 
a new Appendix V, the pro forma Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement (“CRA”). LS Power Grid 
respectfully requests that the Commission accept the proposed tariff revisions to become 
effective January 16, 2027, sixty-one (61) days after filing, consistent with the Commission’s prior 
notice requirement,5 and grant any necessary waivers.

I. 
INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY OF FILING 
The proposed revisions establish a transparent framework for LS Power Grid, a transmission-only, 
non-load-serving Participating Transmission Owner (“PTO”) in the California Independent System 
Operator Corporation (“CAISO”), to interconnect Large Loads and to recover the costs of 
transmission upgrades that are driven, in whole or in part, by a Large Load (“Large Load-Driven 
Upgrades”). New Section 10A and the LLIP in Appendix VI govern ECLL applications, studies, 
interim service, and interconnection agreements. The pro forma CRA in Appendix V establishes 
the Eligible Customer’s twenty-year Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution (“MTRC”) and 
related payment and security obligations for each Covered Upgrade. Amounts received under a 
CRA are credited to transmission customers through LS Power Grid’s existing Transmission 
Revenue Balancing Account Adjustment (“TRBAA”), and LS Power Grid’s existing Formula Rate 
Template already identifies plant by project and removes TRBAA credits from Formula Rate 
revenue credits. Therefore, those credits are not counted twice and no Formula Rate Template 
changes are required. 
The filing responds to the Show Cause Order’s direction that respondents (1) ensure transparency 
concerning the network upgrade costs to provide transmission service to Eligible Customers on 
behalf of large loads, (2) establish a pro forma cost recovery agreement to mitigate the risk of 
cost shifting among transmission customers, and (3) ensure that such payments are appropriately 
credited toward transmission owners’ transmission revenue requirements.6 The CRA assigns the 
wholesale revenue-support obligation to the Eligible Customer that takes transmission service 
on behalf of the Large Load Facility and backs that obligation with Construction Security, 
Operational Security, and a Termination Fee. The framework is designed to mitigate the risk that 
other customers bear the costs of a Covered Upgrade if the associated Large Load is delayed, 
reduced, or does not materialize, while preserving LS Power Grid’s recovery of its revenue 
requirement through its Formula Rate and the CAISO Transmission Access Charge (“TAC”), and 
without changing CAISO cost allocation. 
The proposed revisions do not change the cost-of-service inputs, return, depreciation, taxes, or 
allocators used to calculate LS Power Grid’s revenue requirement, and no changes are proposed 
to LS Power Grid’s Formula Rate Template (Appendix III), its Formula Rate Implementation 
Protocols (Appendix IV), or Appendix I of the TO Tariff. Once these revisions are accepted, a 
conforming, executed CRA with populated Schedules generally will not require an individual FPA 
section 205 filing, while unexecuted agreements, agreements containing a material deviation, 
and other agreements required by Commission rule or order will be filed with the Commission.7 
 
6  Show Cause Order at P 3. 
7  See Ex. No. LSC-200 (Arzola Testimony); CRA § 5.1.

II. 
BACKGROUND 
A. LS Power Grid and Its Formula Rate 
LS Power Grid is a transmission-only PTO in the CAISO that owns the Gates and Round Mountain 
projects, which CAISO selected LS Power Grid to develop through its competitive solicitation 
process, and is developing additional competitively selected projects. The Gates project is an 
approximately 850 MVAR STATCOM at the Gates Substation in Fresno County, and the Round 
Mountain project is an approximately 530 MVAR STATCOM and associated 500 kV switchyard in 
Shasta County. LS Power Grid is a non-load-serving PTO with no End-Use Customers; it neither 
serves retail load nor has a retail relationship with any customer seeking a Large Load 
interconnection. LS Power Grid’s formula rate consists of its Formula Rate Template (Appendix 
III of the TO Tariff) and its Formula Rate Implementation Protocols (“Protocols”) (Appendix IV of 
the TO Tariff) (together, the “Formula Rate”), which were originally accepted in Docket No. ER21-
195-000 and most recently revised in Docket No. ER26-2665-000. LS Power Grid’s Transmission 
Revenue Requirement (“TRR”) is the sum of its Base Transmission Revenue Requirement (“Base 
TRR”), determined under the Formula Rate, and its TRBAA, and is recovered through the CAISO 
TAC. LS Power Grid already uses the TRBAA to credit customers with revenue it receives outside 
the TAC. 
B. Show Cause Order and Stakeholder Process 
On June 18, 2026, the Commission issued the Show Cause Order, instituting an FPA section 206 
proceeding in Docket No. EL26-71-000 directed to CAISO and its PTOs. The Commission 
preliminarily found that existing tariffs appear to be unjust, unreasonable, or unduly 
discriminatory or preferential because they lack sufficiently clear and consistent provisions to 
address the challenges posed by the rapid growth of large loads and co-location arrangements 
between loads and generating facilities.8 The Commission directed each respondent either to 
show cause why its tariff remains just and reasonable or to explain what tariff changes would 
remedy the identified concerns.9 
Following the Show Cause Order, CAISO convened joint coordination meetings with the PTOs to 
address the Show Cause Order and CAISO’s proposed implementation framework, and LS Power 
Grid participated in those meetings from July through October 2026. LS Power Grid also 
participated in CAISO’s public stakeholder meetings and submitted written comments on CAISO’s 
Straw Proposal, Draft Final Proposal, and Draft Tariff Language asking CAISO to recognize non-
load-serving and affected PTOs expressly and to preserve a meaningful role for those PTOs in the 
interconnection and study process. LS Power Grid further participated in discussions with other 
non-load-serving PTOs, the broader PTO group, and load-serving PTOs addressing the application 
and study process, information sharing, technical coordination, and the allocation and recovery

of costs.10 Those discussions highlighted the need to ensure that an affected PTO has a 
meaningful role in the process even when it does not provide retail service to the requesting 
load. LS Power Grid’s proposal does not displace the separate arrangements that an Eligible 
Customer must enter into with an Affected System Owner for an Affected System Upgrade or 
with the owner of a regional project share owned by another entity.11 
III. 
DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED REVISIONS 
A. Large Load Interconnection Framework (Section 10A and Appendix VI) 
A new Section 10A of the TO Tariff establishes an interconnection process for ECLL 
Interconnections. An ECLL is a Utility Distribution Company or Metered Subsystem that provides 
retail transmission and interconnection service to Large Load End-Users in the CAISO Balancing 
Authority Area, and a Large Load is an End-User located at a single site behind one or more Points 
of Withdrawal from the CAISO Controlled Grid with a peak load of 50 MW or greater. Section 
10A.2 specifies the contents of an ECLL Interconnection Application, including the load ramp 
schedule, site plan, Site Control, permits and approvals, electrical configuration, related requests, 
technical data, and Co-Located Large Load information. Section 10A.3 directs that ECLL 
Interconnection Applications be processed, and ECLL Interconnection Agreements be tendered, 
executed, and filed, under the LLIP in Appendix VI. Section 10A.4 provides for Interim Firm 
Interconnection Service and Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (“FILI”) Service before the 
required facilities are completed. FILI Service is subject to curtailment, including during normal 
operating conditions, and is curtailed before Firm Interconnection Service. Section 10A.5 
addresses Co-Located Large Loads, and Section 10A.6 requires a CRA for Large Load-Driven 
Upgrades.12 
LS Power Grid’s proposed LLIP establishes a Commission-jurisdictional framework under which an 
Eligible Customer for Large Load may request Flexible Interim Load Interconnection Service (“FILI 
Service”), subject to study, deﬁned operating limitations, and curtailment by LS Power Grid or 
CAISO as necessary to maintain reliability. The implementing FILI Service Agreement will be 
entered into with LS Power Grid and, as applicable, CAISO, and will establish the applicable 
operating requirements, curtailment conditions, and curtailment implementation mechanism. LS 
Power Grid will work with CAISO and stakeholders to develop a standardized pro forma FILI 
Service Agreement for a subsequent ﬁling. Pending that ﬁling, each FILI Service Agreement will 
be consistent with the LLIP, the applicable Large Load Interconnection Agreement, and CAISO 
Tariﬀ section 25.7.2, and will be ﬁled with the Commission as required under the LLIP and 
applicable law. 
 
10  See Ex. No. LSC-100 (Hayes Testimony). 
11  See CRA §§ 4.2 and 6.3.6. 
12  TO Tariﬀ §§ 3.28 and 3.56.

The LLIP applies to new Large Loads, capacity increases to Large Loads previously processed 
under the LLIP, and increases of 50 MW or greater to existing loads not previously processed 
under the LLIP, for completed Interconnection Requests submitted after Appendix VI becomes 
effective. It provides for a scoping meeting, a Large Load Study Process Agreement, and a Large 
Load Interconnection Study subject to CAISO review and concurrence, with a ninety-Calendar-
Day reasonable-efforts study period. The study must consider alternative transmission 
technologies, including dynamic line ratings, advanced power flow control devices, advanced 
conductors, and transmission switching, and, if traditional network upgrades are selected, the 
PTO must demonstrate why alternative transmission technologies are not feasible or would not 
result in lower costs or a faster timeline.13 The LLIP also establishes financial readiness 
requirements, including a $250,000 Interconnection Study Deposit, Commercial Readiness 
Deposits that bring the aggregate deposit to twenty percent (20%) of the estimated construction 
cost of the Large Load Network Upgrades attributable to the request, and withdrawal penalties, 
and coordinates those deposits with the CRA so that the same costs are not secured twice.14 
The existing Section 10 is retitled the Transmission System Wholesale Load (“TSWL”) 
Interconnection Process and continues to govern TSWL Interconnections. Section 10.1 directs 
ECLL requests to Section 10A, and revised Section 10.9 provides that, where a TSWL 
Interconnection will serve one or more Large Loads, the Eligible Customer taking or requesting 
transmission service on behalf of the Large Load must execute and maintain a CRA, or request 
that it be filed unexecuted, as a condition to LS Power Grid’s design, procurement, construction, 
or operation of any associated Large Load-Driven Upgrades. Section 3 adds definitions for, among 
other terms, Co-Located Large Load, Cost Recovery Agreement, ECLL, ECLL Interconnection, Firm 
Interconnection Service, FILI Service, Interim Firm Interconnection Service, Large Load, Point of 
Withdrawal, Site Control, and TSWL Interconnection, and renumbers the existing definitions. 
B. Pro Forma CRA (Appendix V) 
The pro forma CRA is a contract between LS Power Grid, as Transmission Owner, and the Eligible 
Customer taking wholesale transmission service under the CAISO Tariff on behalf of a Large Load 
Customer. Assigning the payment obligation to that Eligible Customer preserves the wholesale 
obligor structure and does not establish a FERC-jurisdictional retail rate or payment obligation for 
the Large Load Customer. The Large Load Customer executes a Limited Acknowledgment for 
information, authorization, notice, and cooperation purposes, but is not a party to the wholesale 
payment obligations. CAISO is not a party to the CRA, and the CRA creates no obligation of CAISO. 
Covered Upgrades include Large Load-Driven Upgrades and any LS Power Grid-owned share of a 
CAISO-Assigned Regional Project identified in the applicable Schedules for which an Annual MTRC 
is established; Affected System Upgrades and regional project shares owned by another entity 
are addressed through separate arrangements. Where LS Power Grid requires a CRA, Section 10.9

(for a TSWL Interconnection) and LLIP Section 5.3, incorporated through Section 10A.6 (for an 
ECLL Interconnection), require the applicable Eligible Customer to execute it, or to request that 
it be filed unexecuted, within the applicable interconnection-agreement execution period.15 
For each Covered Upgrade, the CRA establishes an Annual MTRC calculated solely under the 
MTRC Calculation Template in Schedule 5, separately from the Formula Rate. The Estimated 
Annual MTRC uses then-current estimated capital cost. Within one year after the Covered 
Upgrade enters service, when actual capital cost is known, LS Power Grid establishes the Final 
Annual MTRC as the final incurred capital cost multiplied by the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed 
Charge Rate calculated under Schedule 5 using the applicable capital structure, cost of debt, 
return on equity, income-tax inputs, a fixed five percent (5%) annual levelized-depreciation 
schedule, and the fixed expense allocator. The MTRC Term begins on the applicable in-service 
date and ends on the day immediately preceding its twentieth anniversary, with partial Rate 
Years prorated. The Final Annual MTRC is not recalculated through the Formula Rate and may 
change only as permitted by Section 6.3.1, including to correct error or fraud, to implement an 
effective prospective reassignment or a final Commission order, or to reflect prospectively a 
Commission-approved change in LS Power Grid’s return on equity or subsequently enacted tax 
rates or tax law.16 
The twenty-year MTRC Term is a defined contractual revenue-support period, not the 
depreciable life of a Covered Upgrade. Each Covered Upgrade placed under CAISO’s Operational 
Control remains in LS Power Grid’s rate base and Base TRR and is subject to ordinary Formula 
Rate treatment. Where an upgrade is driven by more than one Large Load, Schedule 1 identifies 
an Initial Allocation Percentage for each Large Load Customer using the applicable final study and 
allocation methodology, accounting for loads studied individually, jointly, or in a cluster and for 
any portion of the facility that serves other transmission system needs or customers. The 
aggregate Annual MTRC allocated to all Large Load Customers may not exceed one hundred 
percent (100%) of the Annual MTRC for that Covered Upgrade; any unallocated portion remains 
subject to otherwise applicable CAISO cost-allocation and rate-recovery requirements. Each 
allocation percentage is applied only once in calculating the Annual MTRC.17 
The Eligible Customer pays a Supplemental MTRC equal to the greater of zero and the applicable 
Annual MTRC less Qualifying Transmission Revenues (“QTR”). QTR consists of wholesale 
transmission revenues attributable to service to the Large Load Facility that reduce transmission 
revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers or directly credit LS Power Grid’s Net 
Revenue Requirement. As applicable, QTR includes the portion of TAC revenues attributable to 
the Large Load Facility and allocable to LS Power Grid under the reproducible methodology in 
Schedule 2, qualifying Wheeling Access Charges, and other wholesale transmission-access,

wheeling, or transmission-service charges, including charges paid through a non-PTO serving 
entity, without duplicate recognition. The Annual MTRC therefore operates as a revenue floor, 
not an additive charge or separate capacity-reservation commitment. LS Power Grid invoices the 
forecast Supplemental MTRC, including any prior-period true-up adjustment, in monthly 
installments following each Annual Projection, and serves a Reconciliation Statement with each 
Annual Update using actual QTR. Under-billed or over-billed amounts are carried into billing 
following the next Annual Projection, without interest between LS Power Grid and the Eligible 
Customer.18 
Section 6.7 of the CRA establishes for each Covered Upgrade a Total Required Revenue 
Commitment equal to the Final Annual MTRC multiplied by twenty, which is reduced by QTR, 
Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security Proceeds, and other permitted amounts, without 
double counting, and tracked in an upgrade-specific Cumulative Revenue Ledger. Cancellation, 
downsizing, curtailment, or cessation after an applicable in-service date does not itself eliminate 
the Eligible Customer’s obligations. Upon effective termination of the CRA or permanent 
cessation of service after that date, the Eligible Customer owes a lump-sum Termination Fee 
equal to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, less any Supplemental MTRC billed 
and unpaid as of the effective termination or cessation date, which remains separately payable 
and secured. The Termination Fee is an accelerated contractual termination charge, not a 
penalty. LS Power Grid holds each Termination Fee in a separately identified, interest-bearing 
Termination Fee Account and credits it to transmission customers through the TRBAA as Annual 
Termination Fee Credits equal to the Annual MTRC for each remaining Rate Year of the MTRC 
Term. The uncredited balance is accounted for as a deferred liability and is not included in rate 
base.19 
Article 7 of the CRA requires Construction Security for incurred and irrevocably committed costs 
and Pre-In-Service Termination Costs, including applicable cancellation, demobilization, and 
restoration costs and properly accrued allowance for funds used during construction. 
Operational Security must be delivered no later than thirty Calendar Days before the earliest 
expected in-service date and equals one hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining 
Cumulative Revenue Responsibility. Consistent with the Commission’s decision to reduce 
unnecessary redundancy by allowing an Eligible Customer to rely on credit support posted by a 
large load under a retail agreement, direct Operational Security is reduced dollar-for-dollar by 
Qualifying Retail Security Support identified in a currently effective Retail Security Certification. 
That reduction does not reduce the underlying wholesale obligation and does not apply to 
Construction Security or Pre-In-Service Termination Costs. Security does not cap the Eligible 
Customer’s liability. Construction Security provided under an interconnection or engineering and 
procurement agreement for the same costs counts toward, and is not duplicated by, the CRA

required CRA Construction Security only if it is in a form permitted under Schedule 3 and LS Power 
Grid elects that treatment in writing; no amount may be applied or credited more than once.21 
This ﬁling adopts the conservative requirement that direct Operational Security equal one 
hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, subject 
only to Qualifying Retail Security Support. LS Power Grid expects to work with CAISO and 
interested stakeholders to evaluate whether, and under what objectively deﬁned circumstances, 
a lower requirement or another credit-support structure could provide comparable protection 
against cost shifting. Any future change would be submitted to the Commission for review under 
FPA section 205. 
C. Crediting CRA Amounts Through the TRBAA (Sections 3 and 5.3) 
CRA amounts are credited to transmission customers through LS Power Grid’s existing TRBAA, not 
as Formula Rate revenue credits. Because the TO Tariﬀ deﬁnes Transmission Revenue Credits as 
amounts received from, or charges imposed by, CAISO, LS Power Grid proposes to revise the 
deﬁnitions of the Transmission Revenue Balancing Account (“TRBA”) (Section 3.97) and the 
TRBAA (Section 3.98) and Section 5.3 so that the TRBAA also ﬂows through to transmission 
customers all amounts that a CRA requires to be credited through it. The revisions clarify that 
Section 5.3 does not require the payment of interest between LS Power Grid and a party to a CRA, 
which is governed solely by the CRA, and the deﬁnition of Interest (Section 3.54) is revised to the 
same eﬀect. The deﬁnition of Transmission Revenue Credits is unchanged.22 
Each October, LS Power Grid will include a Forecast TRBAA Credit equal to the projected 
Supplemental MTRC for the following year, increased or reduced by any prior-period true-up 
adjustment, plus any Annual Termination Fee Credit scheduled for that year. The Forecast TRBAA 
Credit lowers the TRR eﬀective January 1 and, through the TAC, the transmission charges paid by 
all customers, while the Eligible Customer pays the Supplemental MTRC directly to LS Power Grid. 
Supplemental MTRC cash receipts, Applied Security Proceeds applied to Supplemental MTRC 
obligations, Annual Termination Fee Credits, and any duplicate-recovery credits are recorded in 
the TRBA. A billed but unpaid Supplemental MTRC is not a TRBAA Credit. If LS Power Grid later 
receives payment or applies Security proceeds to that obligation, the amount is recorded only in 
the Rate Year in which it is received or applied. Any diﬀerence between the Forecast TRBAA Credit 
and the actual amounts recorded in the TRBA is reﬂected in the TRBA principal balance and 
ﬂowed through in subsequent TRBAA. QTR is not credited again, and posting, drawing, or holding 
Security does not itself produce a credit. The Eligible Customer remains liable for unpaid Large 
Load Charges, and the CRA’s Security and collection provisions mitigate, but do not eliminate,

its Base TRR, LS Power Grid retains none of the TRBAA Credits.23 
LS Power Grid’s annual TRBAA ﬁling is made under FPA section 205 and is noticed by the 
Commission, open to intervention, comment, and protest, and subject to Commission review and 
acceptance. LS Power Grid will include in each ﬁling the calculations, workpapers, and testimony 
supporting the TRBAA Credits, substantially in the form of Exhibit No. LSC-202, with customer-
speciﬁc information presented on an aggregated basis or submitted with a request for privileged 
treatment under 18 C.F.R. § 388.112. No change to Appendix I is required because TRBAA Credits 
are included in the TRBAA amount stated in Appendix I each year.24 
Balances in the TRBA attributable to CRA amounts accrue interest in the same manner as other 
TRBA balances, because a balance created by a late payment, a non-payment before Security is 
applied, or the timing of monthly installments reﬂects an actual over- or under-recovery by LS 
Power Grid. By contrast, when further Supplemental MTRC will be invoiced, a prior-period true-
up adjustment is added both to the Supplemental MTRC invoiced for a later Rate Year and to the 
Forecast TRBAA Credit for that same year, so the matched adjustment does not itself create an 
over- or under-recovery. Consistent with Section 6.6 of the CRA and Section 5.3 of the TO Tariﬀ, 
no interest accrues on a prior-period true-up adjustment between LS Power Grid and the Eligible 
Customer.25 
D. Formula Rate Template and Rate Treatment of Covered Upgrades 
No changes to LS Power Grid’s Formula Rate Template or Protocols are required. LS Power Grid’s 
existing Attachment 1a – Project Plant Detail Worksheet already reports plant separately by 
project, and Attachment 1 – Project Revenue Requirement Worksheet calculates each project’s 
revenue requirement using the applicable allocation factors, so each Covered Upgrade can be 
reported as a separate project on those worksheets. Attachment 9 – Revenue Credit Detail, Line 
18, “Less: Revenue Credits included in the TRBAA,” removes any TRBAA Credits otherwise 
recorded in the revenue accounts included on Attachment 9, so those amounts are credited to 
customers once, through the TRBAA, and not also through the Formula Rate. The full eligible cost 
of each Covered Upgrade therefore remains in the Base TRR. The existing Protocols govern the 
supporting documentation, information exchange, review, challenge, and true-up of Formula 
Rate inputs, including Covered Upgrade plant and the amounts removed on Attachment 9, Line 
18.26 
Covered Upgrades placed under CAISO’s Operational Control are included in LS Power Grid’s rate 
base and Base TRR in the same manner as other LS Power Grid transmission plant and are subject 
to LS Power Grid’s Commission-accepted Formula Rate, including any generally applicable 
Commission-approved return incentive. Covered Upgrades are not subject to the commitments

E. Supporting Testimony and Illustrative Exhibits 
Mr. Patrick Hayes’ testimony (Exhibit No. LSC-100) describes the Show Cause Order, the CAISO 
stakeholder process, the pro forma CRA, and the associated TO Tariff revisions, and explains how 
those measures assign cost responsibility for Large Load-Driven Upgrades, mitigate cost shifting 
and stranded-asset risk, avoid double recovery, and promote transparency. His supporting 
exhibits provide an Illustrative MTRC Calculation (Exhibit No. LSC-101), an Example Reconciliation 
Statement (Exhibit No. LSC-102), and an Example Invoice Statement (Exhibit No. LSC-103). 
Mr. D. Eric Arzola’s testimony (Exhibit No. LSC-200) explains the crediting of CRA amounts 
through the TRBAA and the related TO Tariff revisions, and explains why no changes are needed 
to the Formula Rate Template, the Protocols, or Appendix I. His supporting exhibits include an 
Illustrative Formula Rate Template populated with hypothetical data for the 2030 Rate Year 
(Exhibit No. LSC-201) and an Illustrative TRBAA Calculation for the TRBA years ending September 
30, 2030 and 2031 (Exhibit No. LSC-202). Using a hypothetical $60 million Covered Upgrade with 
an Annual MTRC of $10,278,360, projected QTR of $3,363,840, and a Supplemental MTRC of 
$6,914,520, those exhibits demonstrate that the TRBAA Credits are removed on Attachment 9, 
Line 18 and returned to customers through the TRBAA, so that they are credited only once. 
IV. 
THE PROPOSED REVISIONS ARE JUST AND REASONABLE 
LS Power Grid’s approach materially mitigates the cost-shifting concern identified in the Show 
Cause Order. Before in-service, LLIP deposits, Construction Security, and the Pre-In-Service 
Termination Cost provisions protect against cancellation and related exposure. After an upgrade 
enters service, the Annual MTRC, Supplemental MTRC, Total Required Revenue Commitment, 
Required Operational Security, and Termination Fee establish and secure a defined twenty-year 
revenue responsibility tied to the allocated capital cost of the identified Covered Upgrades. That 
design responds to the concern that bilateral revenue contributions “untethered from any

The proposal also supplies the transparency and crediting mechanisms the Commission

Crediting CRA amounts through the TRBAA ensures that Large Load payments are credited 
toward LS Power Grid’s TRR. The full cost of each Covered Upgrade remains in the Base TRR,

the TRR, while the TRBAA reduces the TRR paid by all customers through the TAC by the amounts 
received under the CRA. The TRBA ensures that LS Power Grid collects no more and no less than 
its Base TRR, and Attachment 9, Line 18 ensures that each dollar is credited only once. The CRA 
does not alter CAISO cost allocation or the retail arrangements between an Eligible Customer and 
a Large Load Customer. 
Finally, the proposal is appropriately tailored to LS Power Grid as a non-load-serving PTO. It gives 
LS Power Grid a meaningful interconnection and cost-recovery role when a Large Load affects its 
facilities, even though LS Power Grid has no retail relationship with the load, and requires 
evaluation of alternative transmission technologies before traditional network upgrades are 
selected, consistent with the Commission’s focus on keeping costs at a responsible and 
accountable level. It does not disturb the Gates and Round Mountain projects, LS Power Grid’s 
existing revenue requirement, CAISO cost allocation, or CAISO’s study and planning authority.

The TRBAA shall be equal to: 
TRBAA = Cr + Cf + I 
Where: 
 
Cr =  The principal balance in the Transmission Revenue Balancing Account 
(“TRBA”) recorded in FERC Account No. 254 as of September 30 of the

Cost Recovery Agreement, and any over- or under-recovery of its annual 
Transmission Revenue Requirement and the amount of such revenues or 
expenditures that has been refunded to or collected from customers 
through operation of the TRBAA; 
 
Cf =  The forecast of Transmission Revenue Credits, if any, for the 
following calendar year, plus any forecast credit that a Cost Recovery 
Agreement requires to be included in the TRBAA for the following 
calendar year; 
 
I =  
The interest balance for the TRBA, which shall be calculated using the 
interest rate pursuant to Section 35.19a of FERC’s regulations under the 
Federal Power Act (18 CFR Section 35.19a). Interest shall be calculated 
based on the average TRBA principal balance each month, compounded

6.9. 
Prospective Reassignment of Revenue Responsibility.  
6.9.1. Eligibility for Reassignment of Revenue Responsibility. Whether or not the 
Large Load Customer remains in service, a portion of the prospective revenue 
responsibility associated with a Large Load-Driven Upgrade may be reassigned to a 
subsequent load customer if an objective transmission study conducted under the 
applicable tariff or study process determines that: 
(a) the subsequent large load customer relies upon identifiable incremental 
capability created by the Large Load-Driven Upgrade; and 
(b) that reliance avoids or reduces identifiable transmission upgrades that 
otherwise would have been required to provide the subsequent large load 
customer’s requested service. 
Incidental power flows, generalized system benefits, or use of the transmission 
system that does not satisfy both requirements shall not support a reassignment. 
This Section 6.9 applies only to a load customer other than the Large Load 
Customer, at a facility other than the Large Load Facility. It does not apply to a 
transfer of ownership or operation of the Large Load Facility, a change in Eligible 
Customer, or an assignment of this Agreement, which are governed by Sections 
6.10 and 10.1 and do not alter the Applicable Allocation Percentage or the Large 
Load-Driven Upgrades attributable to the Large Load Facility. 
6.9.2. Reassignment Calculation. LS Power Grid shall determine the prospective 
reassignment separately for each Large Load-Driven Upgrade satisfying Section 
6.9.1 (each, a “Shared Upgrade”). For each Shared Upgrade: 
(a) the Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost shall equal the reasonable 
estimated cost of the transmission upgrades that would have been required 
for the subsequent large load customer absent the Shared Upgrade, less the 
reasonable estimated cost of any additional transmission upgrades required 
when the capability of the Shared Upgrade is considered; 
(b) the Remaining Allocated Net Plant shall equal the portion of the Shared 
Upgrade’s net plant balance included in rate base immediately before the 
reassignment that remains assigned to the Large Load Customer under this 
Agreement; 
(c) the Capability-Supported Amount shall equal the portion of the Remaining 
Allocated Net Plant reasonably attributable to the incremental capability of

29 
 
the Shared Upgrade actually relied upon by the subsequent large load 
customer; and 
(d) the Reassigned Investment Amount shall equal the least of: 
(i) the Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost; 
(ii) the Capability-Supported Amount; and 
(iii) the Remaining Allocated Net Plant. 
The Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost, Capability-Supported Amount, and 
Remaining Allocated Net Plant shall be determined using a consistent cost basis and 
price year. If Remaining Allocated Net Plant is greater than zero, the Reassignment 
Percentage shall equal the Reassigned Investment Amount divided by the 
Remaining Allocated Net Plant, bounded between zero and one hundred percent 
(100%). If Remaining Allocated Net Plant is zero or negative, no Reassignment 
Percentage shall be calculated under this methodology; any reassignment shall 
require an applicable tariff methodology or Commission determination addressing 
that circumstance. 
6.9.3. Prospective Adjustment of Revenue Responsibility. Beginning on the 
Reassignment Effective Date, the applicable Annual MTRC assigned to the Large 
Load Customer shall be prospectively reduced by the Reassignment Percentage 
applied to the Shared Upgrade. LS Power Grid shall record a separate effective 
prospective reassignment credit in the Cumulative Revenue Ledger equal to the 
Reassignment Percentage multiplied by the Remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility associated with the Shared Upgrade that remains assigned to the 
Large Load Customer immediately before the Reassignment Effective Date. That 
credit shall be the sole Cumulative Revenue Ledger adjustment for the reassigned 
responsibility. It shall not adjust the Total Required Revenue Commitment or result 
in a second reduction to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility or 
Required Operational Security for the same reassigned responsibility. 
LS Power Grid shall recalculate the Supplemental MTRC and Operational Security 
under this Agreement to reflect the reassignment. The Reassignment Effective Date 
shall be the latest of: 
(a) the date the subsequent large load customer commences the service for 
which the Shared Upgrade provides the identified incremental capability; 
(b) the effective date of a cost recovery agreement establishing the subsequent 
large load customer’s corresponding revenue responsibility; 
(c) the date on which all Security required from the eligible customer serving 
the subsequent large load customer becomes effective; and 
(d) the date on which the study and any other approvals required under the 
applicable tariff become final. 
No reduction in the Large Load Customer’s Operational Security shall occur until 
the corresponding responsibility and required Security have become effective for the 
subsequent large load customer.

30 
 
6.9.4. Prospective Treatment and Prevention of Duplicate Reassignment. A 
reassignment under this Section shall: 
(a) operate prospectively only and shall not produce a refund, credit, or 
reopening of amounts properly determined for a prior Rate Year; 
(b) transfer prospective revenue responsibility only and shall not constitute a 
sale or transfer of transmission facilities, a transfer of plant ownership, a 
change in plant accounting, or a modification of any CAISO cost allocation; 
(c) not exceed the prospective responsibility remaining under this Agreement 
for the Shared Upgrade; and 
(d) not assign the same transmission capability, avoided upgrade cost, Annual 
MTRC, or Cumulative Revenue Responsibility to more than one large load 
customer. 
LS Power Grid shall maintain an upgrade-specific reassignment ledger identifying 
the capability and responsibility assigned to each large load customer. Once 
responsibility has been effectively reassigned, that responsibility shall not revert to 
the Large Load Customer if the subsequent large load customer later terminates, 
reduces, or fails to commence service. The reassigned responsibility shall instead 
remain with the subsequent large load customer and the Eligible Customer 
responsible for its payment, subject to any further prospective reassignment 
permitted under the applicable agreement and tariff. 
Any prospective reassignment, adjustment, or change in the cost share of a CAISO-
Assigned Regional Project shall be recognized under this Agreement only to the 
extent authorized or required by the CAISO Tariff or a Commission-accepted 
methodology. LS Power Grid shall apply an effective change prospectively to the 
Regional Project Allocated ARR, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, 
Supplemental MTRC, TRBAA Credit, and Operational Security, and shall update 
Schedule 4 and the applicable workpapers. The change shall not assign the same 
project share to more than one customer or alter costs allocated to other customers 
under the CAISO Tariff.

6.9 and does not require a study under Section 6.9.1. Cost responsibility shall continue 
to follow the Large Load Facility, the transferee shall execute a Limited 
Acknowledgment substantially in the form included in this Agreement, and Eligible 
Customer shall remain responsible for its obligations under this Agreement unless they 
are transferred to a Successor Eligible Customer under this Section 6.10. 
6.11. CAISO Data and Settlement Coordination. Eligible Customer shall provide LS 
Power Grid, or authorize and direct its Scheduling Coordinator, Utility Distribution 
Company, Metering Coordinator, and other applicable entities to provide LS Power 
Grid, with the metering, settlement, billing, resettlement, allocation, and other data 
reasonably necessary to calculate and verify Qualifying Transmission Revenues and 
administer this Agreement. Eligible Customer shall execute any authorization or data-
release documentation reasonably necessary for LS Power Grid to obtain such 
information. 
To the extent authorized or required by the CAISO Tariff, CAISO may provide or 
make available relevant settlement, metering, billing, resettlement, and allocation data 
as provided under the CAISO Requirements. Nothing in this Agreement, however, 
imposes an obligation on CAISO or makes CAISO a party to this Agreement. LS 
Power Grid and Eligible Customer shall cooperate with CAISO and other applicable 
entities to establish and maintain the billing identifiers, metering points, data 
exchanges, and authorizations identified in Schedule 2. 
LS Power Grid shall calculate Qualifying Transmission Revenues, the Annual MTRC, 
and the Supplemental MTRC; maintain the Cumulative Revenue Ledger; and serve on 
Eligible Customer the Reconciliation Statement, including the Cumulative Revenue 
Ledger statement, required by Sections 6.6 and 6.7. 
If final data are not available when a calculation is required, LS Power Grid may use 
reasonable estimates based on the best information then available, subject to 
reconciliation under Section 6.6 when final or corrected data become available.

shall provide Eligible Customer the workpapers, data, and other information 
reasonably necessary to verify the identification of Large Load-Driven Upgrades and

Regional Project Allocated ARR, Total Required Revenue Commitment, Qualifying 
Transmission Revenues, Supplemental MTRC, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, 
TRBAA Credits, reassignment, and Security under this Agreement. Any dispute 
concerning those matters shall be resolved under Article 11. Large Load Customer and 
any Successor Eligible Customer may participate in a dispute under Article 11 to the

32 
 
extent the dispute affects its obligations under this Agreement or its Limited 
Acknowledgment. Customer-specific information shall be protected under Section 
16.3 of the TO Tariff, the CAISO Tariff, and any applicable confidentiality agreement. 
7. Security and Payment Obligations 
7.1. 
Construction Security. Before an applicable Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaches its 
Upgrade In-Service Date, Eligible Customer shall maintain Construction Security 
under the relevant agreement sufficient to secure: 
(a) LS Power Grid’s incurred and irrevocably committed engineering, design, 
procurement, permitting, construction, testing, and related costs attributable 
to that upgrade; and 
(b) the Pre-In-Service Termination Costs described in Section 3.3.2, including 
properly accrued AFUDC and applicable cancellation, demobilization, 
equipment removal, disposition, remediation, and restoration costs 
(“Construction Security”).  
Construction Security secures, but does not limit, Eligible Customer’s liability for 
those amounts. Construction Security provided under the relevant Interconnection 
Agreement or an engineering and procurement agreement for the same costs shall 
count toward, and shall not be duplicated by, the Construction Security required under 
this Agreement. Construction Security shall remain in effect for each Large Load-
Driven Upgrade until that upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date and the 
applicable release or conversion conditions in Section 7.2 are satisfied. 
A Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaching its Upgrade In-Service Date shall not result in 
the release of Construction Security attributable to another Large Load-Driven 
Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date. Eligible Customer shall 
replenish Construction Security within ten (10) Business Days after notice of a 
permitted draw and supporting information if additional secured obligations remain 
and the remaining Construction Security is less than the amount required under this 
Section. 
For a CAISO-Assigned Regional Project owned by LS Power Grid, any pre-service 
payment, contribution, or security required from Eligible Customer for its formally 
assigned share shall be provided only as required by the CAISO Tariff, an applicable 
Interconnection Agreement, or another Commission-accepted arrangement, and shall 
be identified in Schedule 4. This Agreement does not independently require pre-
service Construction Security solely because CAISO has assigned a share of a regional 
project to the Large Load Facility. The treatment of costs for a cancelled or abandoned 
regional project shall be governed by Section 6.3.5 and the applicable Commission 
order, CAISO Tariff, and any project-specific abandoned-plant incentive authorized by 
the Commission. For a project owned by another entity, construction and operational 
security shall be provided under the CAISO Tariff or the arrangement required by 
Section 6.3.6 and Schedule 4; it shall not be treated as LS Power Grid Operational

33 
 
Security unless included in LS Power Grid’s Formula Rate and expressly identified as 
LS Power Grid’s share. 
7.2. 
Delivery of Operational Security. No later than thirty (30) Calendar Days before the 
earliest expected Upgrade In-Service Date identified in Schedule 1 or Regional Project 
In-Service Date identified in Schedule 4 for a LS Power Grid-owned CAISO-Assigned 
Regional Project, Eligible Customer shall deliver Operational Security calculated 
under this Article for the Large Load-Driven Upgrades and LS Power Grid-owned 
CAISO-Assigned Regional Project expected to enter service. Operational Security 
must be fully effective before any applicable Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional 
Project In-Service Date.  
If different Large Load-Driven Upgrades or LS Power Grid-owned CAISO-Assigned 
Regional Projects are expected to reach their applicable in-service dates on different 
dates, LS Power Grid shall recalculate the Required Operational Security before each 
subsequent in-service date to include the additional Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility attributable to the upgrade or project share entering service. Eligible 
Customer shall provide any resulting increase no later than fifteen (15) Business Days 
after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if earlier. 
Inclusion of pre-service Construction Work in Progress in rate base shall not constitute 
an Upgrade In-Service Date or independently trigger the Operational Security 
requirement. Construction Security shall remain applicable to each Large Load-Driven 
Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date. 
No Construction Security attributable to a Large Load-Driven Upgrade shall be 
released or converted unless:  
(a) the Required Operational Security attributable to that upgrade is effective; 
(b) that upgrade has reached its Upgrade In-Service Date; and 
(c) LS Power Grid has determined that all Pre-In-Service Termination Costs and 
other construction-related obligations attributable to that upgrade have been 
paid or adequately reserved for. 
Any portion of Construction Security retained for unresolved construction costs shall 
be released after LS Power Grid determines that those costs have been paid or 
adequately reserved for or, if Section 3.3.2 applies, after the Termination Cost 
Reconciliation becomes final. Failure to timely deliver Required Operational Security 
is a default permitting LS Power Grid, to the extent authorized by the applicable tariffs 
and agreements, to suspend energization or service, terminate applicable 
interconnection arrangements, and draw Construction Security for secured obligations.  
7.3. 
Required Operational Security. Required Operational Security shall equal one 
hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility. LS Power Grid shall reduce that amount only by the portion of 
Qualifying Retail Security Support identified in a currently effective Retail Security 
Certification. A Retail Security Certification is accepted in reliance on Eligible

34 
 
Customer’s representations and does not require LS Power Grid to review the 
underlying retail-security documents in the ordinary course. If LS Power Grid has a 
reasonable basis to question the certification, or after a payment default, Credit 
Review Event, or Material Adverse Credit Event, LS Power Grid may request 
supporting information reasonably necessary to verify continued compliance. Any 
resulting deficiency shall be delivered or restored within fifteen (15) Business Days 
after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if earlier. 
7.4. 
Annual Resizing and Security Notices. LS Power Grid shall recalculate Required 
Operational Security with each Annual Projection, Final MTRC Determination Date, 
recalculation of a Final Annual MTRC under Section 6.3.1, Reconciliation Statement, 
effective prospective reassignment, replacement or expiration of Qualifying Retail 
Security Support, or Credit Review Event. If LS Power Grid reasonably determines 
that the Required Security Amount exceeds available Security, it may issue a Security 
Notice identifying the required increase or restoration and reasonable supporting detail 
then available. Eligible Customer shall provide the required increase or restoration 
within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the Security Notice, or by the 
applicable in-service date if earlier. A reduction shall be released only after the 
relevant calculation and reconciliation are final. 
7.5. 
Form of Operational Security. Except to the extent of currently effective Qualifying 
Retail Security Support, Eligible Customer shall provide direct Operational Security in 
the form of cash, an irrevocable standby Letter of Credit meeting Schedule 3, or any 
combination of cash and Letter of Credit. LS Power Grid may accept another form of 
Security that it determines, in its sole discretion, is acceptable. 
Each Letter of Credit shall have an initial stated term of at least twelve (12) months 
and shall remain continuously effective until released under this Agreement; provided, 
however, that a Letter of Credit may have a stated expiration date before its release 
date if Eligible Customer timely extends or replaces it so that Security in an amount 
not less than the Required Security Amount remains continuously available to LS 
Power Grid.  
If an issuing bank has the right not to renew a Letter of Credit, the Letter of Credit 
shall require the issuing bank to provide LS Power Grid and Eligible Customer at least 
ninety (90) Calendar Days’ prior written notice of nonrenewal. Eligible Customer shall 
provide a conforming extension or replacement Letter of Credit, or additional cash 
collateral or other Security accepted by LS Power Grid, no later than sixty (60) 
Calendar Days before the applicable expiration date.   
If Eligible Customer fails to provide the required extension, replacement, or other 
Security by that deadline, LS Power Grid may, before the Letter of Credit expires, 
draw all or any portion of the then-available amount under the Letter of Credit and 
retain the proceeds as cash collateral, apply the proceeds to secured obligations, or 
both. Any proceeds retained but not applied shall continue to constitute Security until 
released under this Agreement.

35 
 
7.6. 
Draw and Application. LS Power Grid may draw against all or any portion of a 
Letter of Credit, apply cash collateral, or apply another form of Security accepted by 
LS Power Grid to secured obligations upon: (a) an unpaid Supplemental MTRC, true-
up, Termination Fee, or other amount due after the applicable payment period; (b) 
Eligible Customer’s failure to timely deliver, maintain, replace, restore, or increase 
Security; (c) cancellation, termination, withdrawal, abandonment, or permanent 
cessation of the Large Load Facility or a material breach of this Agreement; (d) a 
material inaccuracy in a Retail Security Certification or Security instrument; (e) 
Eligible Customer: (i) files a voluntary petition in bankruptcy or seeks reorganization, 
arrangement, or similar relief under any bankruptcy, insolvency, or debtor-relief law; 
(ii) becomes subject to an involuntary bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding that is not 
dismissed within sixty (60) Calendar Days; (iii) has a receiver, trustee, liquidator, or 
custodian appointed for it or a substantial portion of its assets, which appointment is 
not vacated within sixty (60) Calendar Days; (iv) makes a general assignment for the 
benefit of creditors; or (v) admits in writing its inability to pay debts as they become 
due; or (f) Eligible Customer fails to extend, replace, or otherwise maintain Security in 
the amount and within the time required by Section 7.5, including following a notice 
of nonrenewal, issuer rating reduction, or other event affecting the availability of a 
Letter of Credit. 
A draw shall not automatically require replenishment to the amount maintained 
immediately before the draw. Following any application of drawn proceeds to an 
amount due, LS Power Grid shall recalculate the remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility and the Operational Security then required under this Article. Eligible 
Customer shall replenish only the amount, if any, by which the remaining Operational 
Security is less than the recalculated Required Security Amount, within fifteen (15) 
Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if 
earlier. 
Proceeds drawn solely to prevent the expiration or nonrenewal of a Letter of Credit, 
and cash collateral not yet applied to an identified payment obligation, shall remain 
refundable Security and shall continue to constitute Operational Security until applied 
to an amount then due or released under Section 7.9. Such proceeds and cash collateral 
shall be included in determining the amount of remaining Operational Security and 
shall not create an additional replenishment obligation merely because they are held by 
LS Power Grid. 
The posting, drawing, holding, replacement, or replenishment of Operational Security 
shall not, by itself, satisfy the secured obligation, reduce Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility, or produce a TRBAA Credit. Drawn proceeds of Operational Security 
shall become Applied Security Proceeds only when LS Power Grid applies them to an 
identified Supplemental MTRC, prior-period true-up adjustment, Termination Fee, or 
other secured payment obligation arising under Article 6 or Section 3.3.4. Upon 
application, the proceeds shall reduce that obligation dollar-for-dollar and shall receive 
the TRBAA treatment required by Section 6.8; provided, however, that Applied 
Security Proceeds applied to a Termination Fee shall be administered under Section 
3.3.4 and credited to transmission customer only through the Annual Termination Fee

36 
 
Credits provided under Section 6.8. Proceeds of Construction Security applied to Pre-
In-Service Termination Costs or other construction-related obligations shall be treated 
as provided in Sections 3.3.2 and 3.3.3. 
7.7. 
Security Maintenance. Because Required Operational Security is initially one 
hundred percent (100%) of nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, 
no separate acceleration concept applies. An incorrect, expired, withdrawn, 
unavailable, or materially misleading Retail Security Certification, or the loss of 
enforceable retail-security rights described in it, is a Material Adverse Credit Event. 
Eligible Customer shall provide replacement direct Security for any resulting 
uncovered amount within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice, 
or by the applicable in-service date if earlier. 
7.8. 
Post-Termination Administration and Cash Collateral. LS Power Grid shall 
continue the annual calculations, invoices, and true-ups required under this Agreement 
following termination of service to, or the departure, permanent cessation, or material 
reduction of service by, the Large Load Customer until the Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility and all other obligations under this Agreement have been finally 
satisfied, transferred, reassigned, refunded, or otherwise resolved. The Parties intend 
that cash collateral and proceeds of Security be treated as a deposit or deferred liability 
rather than as a Contribution in Aid of Construction, customer financing of 
transmission plant, or a reduction to LS Power Grid’s rate base. To the extent 
permitted by applicable Commission accounting and ratemaking requirements and tax 
law, LS Power Grid shall record and administer such amounts as the corresponding 
annual costs and payment obligations arise. The treatment described in this Section is 
subject to the Commission’s Uniform System of Accounts, the Formula Rate, the 
Protocols, applicable Commission orders, and other Applicable Laws and Regulations. 
If the Commission requires a different accounting or ratemaking treatment, LS Power 
Grid shall implement the required treatment and make corresponding adjustments 
necessary to prevent duplicate recovery and preserve, to the extent permitted, the 
economic allocation established by this Agreement. The Parties shall cooperate in 
seeking any necessary Commission authorization or acceptance.  
Nothing in this Agreement guarantees a particular accounting, ratemaking, or tax 
result. Cash collateral and unapplied Security proceeds shall remain subject to release 
under Section 7.9, including release to reflect an effective prospective reassignment 
under Section 6.9. 
7.9. 
Release of Security. LS Power Grid shall release excess Operational Security only 
after the applicable Reconciliation Statement becomes final. LS Power Grid shall 
release Security attributable to an effective prospective reassignment and shall release 
all remaining Security within thirty (30) Calendar Days after final satisfaction of the 
Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and all other secured obligations. Termination 
alone does not require release. 
7.10. Security Does Not Limit Liability. The Required Security Amount is based on LS 
Power Grid’s then-current estimates and calculations and does not cap, replace, or

37 
 
discharge Eligible Customer’s underlying obligations. A shortfall between Security 
and the amount due remains immediately payable to LS Power Grid. 
7.11. Events of Default; Remedies. Each of the following is an “Event of Default” by 
Eligible Customer: (a) failure to pay any undisputed amount when due that continues 
for ten (10) Business Days after written notice from LS Power Grid; (b) failure to 
deliver, maintain, replace, restore, or increase Security when required under this 
Article 7 or Schedule 3 that continues after the applicable cure period; (c) any other 
material breach of this Agreement, including under Section 4.2 or 6.3.6, that continues 
for thirty (30) Calendar Days after written notice from LS Power Grid or, if the breach 
cannot reasonably be cured within that period, for such longer period, not to exceed 
ninety (90) Calendar Days, as Eligible Customer diligently pursues a cure; and (d) any 
event described in Section 7.6(e). Upon an Event of Default, LS Power Grid may, 
subject to Applicable Laws and Regulations and the applicable tariffs and agreements: 
(i) draw and apply Security under Section 7.6; (ii) exercise the rights described in 
Sections 4.2.6 and 7.2; (iii) before the first Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional 
Project In-Service Date, terminate this Agreement under Section 3.3.1; and (iv) pursue 
any other remedy available at law or in equity or before the Commission. No 
termination after an Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional Project In-Service Date 
releases the obligations described in Section 3.3.4. 
8. Force Majeure. 
8.1. 
If a Party is rendered unable, wholly or in part, by Force Majeure to carry out a 
nonmonetary obligation, that obligation shall be suspended only to the extent and for 
the period performance is prevented. Force Majeure does not suspend or excuse 
payment of incurred construction costs, Pre-In-Service Termination Costs, 
Supplemental MTRC, the Termination Fee, prior-period true-up adjustments, or the

event continues for more than twenty (20) Calendar Days in a sixty (60)-Calendar Day

remains subject to Sections 3.4 and 3.5.

10. Assignment 
10.1. Except for a change in Eligible Customer governed by Section 6.10, a Party may 
assign this Agreement only with the other Party’s written consent; provided that a 
Party may assign to an Affiliate with equal or greater creditworthiness and legal and 
operational capacity to perform. No assignment or change in retail service provider 
releases the existing Eligible Customer until the assignee or Successor Eligible 
Customer executes the required assumption, provides required Security, and the

11. Disputes 
All disputes, claims, or controversies arising out of or relating to this Agreement, including 
any dispute concerning the identification or allocation of Large Load-Driven Upgrades or 
Covered Upgrades; any calculation, update, or recalculation of an Estimated Annual MTRC, 
Final Annual MTRC, Regional Project Allocated ARR, or the MTRC Calculation Template; 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues; Supplemental MTRC; Total Required Revenue 
Commitment; Cumulative Revenue Responsibility; TRBAA Credits; Pre-In-Service 
Termination Costs; the Termination Fee; prospective reassignment; or Security, shall be 
resolved under this Article 11, except that a dispute concerning CAISO’s designation of a 
regional project or assignment of a project cost share shall be resolved under the applicable 
CAISO Tariff procedures. Any payment, refund, credit, or other adjustment resulting from the 
resolution of a dispute under this Article 11 shall be implemented as provided in Section 11.5. 
11.1. Submission and Informal Resolution. In the event of a dispute or claim arising out 
of or relating to this Agreement, the disputing Party shall provide the other Party with 
a written notice describing the dispute (“Notice of Dispute”). The dispute shall be 
referred promptly to designated senior representatives for informal resolution. The 
representatives shall meet or confer within ten (10) Business Days and shall use 
reasonable efforts to resolve the matter within thirty (30) Calendar Days after receipt 
of the Notice of Dispute. This informal process is not a condition to seeking 
emergency relief, filing a FERC complaint, or invoking any ADR processes. 
11.2. Alternative Dispute Resolution. If a dispute is not resolved informally, any Party 
may request Alternative Dispute Resolution (“ADR”). The Parties shall use the ADR 
procedures, neutral-selection process, confidentiality protections, and timing 
requirements specified in the applicable FERC rules. ADR shall be conducted by 
persons knowledgeable in electric utility, transmission, and FERC matters and shall 
not alter a jurisdictional rate, term, or condition unless accepted or approved by the 
FERC.

40 
 
11.3. FERC Complaints and Other Rights. Any Party may instead file a complaint, 
petition, or other pleading with the FERC under Section 206 or Section 306 of the 
Federal Power Act, or seek other relief available under the Federal Power Act or 
Applicable Laws and Regulations, and LS Power Grid may make any filing under 
Section 205 of the Federal Power Act permitted by Section 12.12. No Party’s 
participation in informal negotiations or ADR waives or limits its right to seek FERC 
action. A final ADR determination affecting jurisdictional rates, terms, conditions, 
charges, or Network Upgrades shall be filed with the FERC if required. 
11.4. Costs and Interim Performance. Unless otherwise determined through ADR, the 
Parties shall bear their own costs and share neutral costs as specified by the applicable 
ADR procedure. During a dispute, each Party shall continue performing undisputed 
payment and operational obligations, and shall pay undisputed amounts when due.  
11.5. Implementation of Dispute Determinations; TRBAA. Within thirty (30) Calendar 
Days after a dispute under this Article 11 is finally resolved, whether by written 
agreement of the Parties, a final ADR determination (subject to any required 
Commission filing or acceptance), or a final Commission order (each, a “Dispute 
Determination”), LS Power Grid shall: (a) update the affected MTRC Calculation 
Template, Schedules, Cumulative Revenue Ledger, Reconciliation Statement, and 
Required Operational Security, as applicable, and serve the updated documents on 
Eligible Customer; and (b) invoice or refund, as applicable, any amount owed between 
the Parties as a result of the Dispute Determination, without interest. To the extent a 
Dispute Determination changes a TRBAA Credit or any other amount previously 
credited to, or recovered from, transmission customers, including any change in 
Supplemental MTRC Receipts or Applied Security Proceeds for a prior Rate Year, LS 
Power Grid shall record the resulting difference in the TRBA under Section 6.8 and 
flow it through to transmission customers through the TRBAA, and any amount so 
returned by LS Power Grid to transmission customers shall include interest as 
provided in Section 5.3 of the TO Tariff. If a final Commission order in a proceeding 
concerning LS Power Grid’s TRBAA requires a change to any TRBAA Credit 
attributable to this Agreement, LS Power Grid shall implement that order in the TRBA 
and shall make any corresponding updates and adjustments between the Parties under 
this Section 11.5 as if the order were a Dispute Determination. Nothing in this Section 
reopens the Final Annual MTRC or Total Required Revenue Commitment except as 
required to implement a Dispute Determination or as permitted by Section 6.3.1.

(e) the body of this Agreement shall control over a Schedule in the event of a

Schedule 2 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues Methodology 
1. Purpose and Controlling Principles 
This Schedule establishes the reproducible methodology for calculating projected and actual 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues attributable to the Large Load Facility. It is intended to 
identify wholesale transmission revenues paid by or on behalf of Eligible Customer that are 
attributable to the Large Load Facility and reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected 
from CAISO customers or directly credit LS Power Grid’s Net Revenue Requirement. Such 
revenues may include applicable TAC revenues and qualifying Wheeling Access Charges or 
other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or transmission-service charges under the 
CAISO Tariff or another Commission-accepted arrangement, including charges paid through a 
non-PTO serving entity. The Supplemental MTRC therefore measures only the remaining 
shortfall below the applicable Annual MTRC. 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall be counted once in calculating the Supplemental MTRC 
and the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility against the combined Annual MTRC for all Covered 
Upgrades. They shall not also be treated as a TRBAA Credit under Section 6.8 because they 
reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers. This Schedule does 
not modify CAISO settlement rules, establish a retail rate, impose any obligation on CAISO, or 
alter any cost allocation established under the CAISO Requirements.

4. Applicable Withdrawals 
For each CAISO settlement interval or other reproducible billing interval, Applicable 
Withdrawals shall equal the metered energy withdrawals attributable to the Large Load Facility 
at the metering point identified in Section 2 of this Schedule, expressed in MWh and adjusted as 
follows: 
(a) Imports, exports, station service, auxiliary load, behind-the-meter generation, storage 
charging and discharging, and other injections or withdrawals shall be treated 
consistently with the manner in which they are recognized for the applicable TAC charge 
under the CAISO Tariff. 
(b) Distribution losses and transmission losses shall be included only to the extent they are 
included in the billing determinant for the applicable TAC component. The loss factor or 
method shall be identified in the project-specific table in Section 10 of this Schedule. 
(c) If the Large Load Facility shares a meter or settlement identifier with other load, the 
withdrawals attributable to the Large Load Facility shall be determined from revenue-
quality submeters or another objective allocation method identified in Section 10 of this 
Schedule. An allocation based solely on estimates may be used temporarily but shall be 
reconciled when reliable data become available. 
(d) Withdrawals shall not be counted for a period before the corresponding Annual MTRC is 
included in the Supplemental MTRC calculation under Section 6.4 of the Agreement, 
except where necessary to correct a prior-period error or resettlement. 
5. Applicable TAC Revenue 
Applicable TAC Revenue for an interval shall equal Applicable Withdrawals multiplied by the 
CAISO transmission rate or rates actually applicable to those withdrawals for that interval. The 
calculation shall include only transmission charge components that contribute to recovery of the 
revenue requirement in which LS Power Grid’s costs are included. It shall exclude retail 
distribution charges, generation charges, non-transmission surcharges, taxes collected for another 
governmental entity, and any other charge that does not contribute to recovery of LS Power 
Grid’s transmission revenue requirement. 
If CAISO uses a monthly, annual, or other non-interval billing determinant, LS Power Grid shall 
perform the calculation using that same billing period and determinant. If more than one TAC 
rate or component applies, each component shall be calculated separately before applying the LS 
Power Grid Allocation Factor. 
6. LS Power Grid Allocation Factor 
The LS Power Grid Allocation Factor shall identify the portion of Applicable TAC Revenue 
allocable to LS Power Grid for the relevant period. Unless a different Commission-accepted 
method is stated in Section 10 of this Schedule, the factor shall be calculated from the same 
revenue requirement, billing determinant, allocation percentage, and other inputs used by CAISO 
to include LS Power Grid’s net transmission revenue requirement in the applicable TAC rate. 
For each applicable rate component and period:

Schedule 2 - 4 
 
LS Power Grid Allocation Factor = LS Power Grid Net Revenue Requirement included in 
the applicable TAC component ÷ Total Net Revenue Requirement recovered through that 
TAC component. 
If LS Power Grid’s revenue requirement is recovered through a project-specific, zonal, or other 
direct allocation rather than a systemwide factor, the corresponding Commission-accepted 
allocation percentage or rate component shall be used. The supporting workpapers shall identify 
the source and calculation of each factor. 
7. Calculation of Qualifying Transmission Revenues 
Projected and actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall be calculated as follows for each 
applicable interval, month, or billing period and then aggregated for the Rate Year or partial Rate 
Year: 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues =  Qualifying TAC Revenue + Qualifying Wheeling and 
Other Wholesale Transmission Revenues ± Applicable Adjustments. 
Qualifying TAC Revenue = Σ [(Applicable Withdrawals × Applicable TAC Rate) × LS Power 
Grid Allocation Factor]. Qualifying Wheeling and Other Wholesale Transmission Revenues 
equal Wheeling Access Charges and other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or 
transmission-service charges actually paid by or on behalf of Eligible Customer to CAISO, a 
Participating TO, or a non-PTO transmission or load-serving entity for deliveries serving the 
Large Load Facility, but only to the extent those revenues reduce transmission revenues 
otherwise collected through TAC or directly credit LS Power Grid’s Net Revenue Requirement. 
Applicable Adjustments shall include only amounts attributable to the Large Load Facility, 
including CAISO resettlements, billing corrections, refunds, charge reversals, balancing-account 
adjustments, and other adjustments that change the qualifying transmission revenue. Bad debt or

(a) The Annual Projection shall use forecast withdrawals, then-effective or forecast TAC

(c) A change in Eligible Customer, Scheduling Coordinator, or retail service provider shall 
not interrupt the calculation or cause the same withdrawals or revenues to be omitted or 
counted more than once. Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall remain associated with 
the Large Load Customer and Large Load Facility, regardless of which Eligible 
Customer is responsible for payment during the applicable period.

 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION PROCEDURES (LLIP) 
 
 
Section 1. 
Objectives and Applicability  
1.1 Objectives 
 
The objective of this LLIP is to implement requirements for Large Load interconnections to the 
Participating TO’s Transmission System pursuant to the TO Tariff.  For purposes of this LLIP, 
the “Participating TO” is LS Power Grid California, LLC (“LS Power Grid”), and the “TO 
Tariff” is the LS Power Grid California, LLC Transmission Owner Tariff.  Because LS Power 
Grid is a Non-Load-Serving Participating TO and has no End-Use Customers, a Large Load 
interconnecting under this LLIP will not be a retail transmission customer of the Participating 
TO.   
 
1.2 Applicability  
 
The LLIP is applicable to a Large Load Interconnection Customer that is either (1) proposing to 
interconnect a Large Load to the Participating TO’s Transmission System; (2) seeking to 
increase the capacity of an existing Large Load processed under the LLIP; or (3) with respect to 
an existing load interconnected to the Participating TO’s Transmission System that was not 
processed under the LLIP, seeking an increase of 50 MW or greater.  This LLIP only applies to 
completed Interconnection Requests submitted after the effective date of this Appendix VI to the 
TO Tariff.  Consistent with Section 10A of the TO Tariff, all requests for ECLL Interconnection 
shall be directed to the Participating TO.  An Interconnection Request submitted under this LLIP 
shall constitute the ECLL Interconnection Application, and the Interconnection Studies and the 
Large Load Interconnection Agreement under this LLIP shall constitute the study process and 
the ECLL Interconnection Agreement, respectively, for purposes of Section 10A of the TO 
Tariff.

singular of any definition shall include the plural and the plural shall include the singular.  If a 
term with initial capitalization used herein is not defined, such term shall have the meanings 
ascribed to such term in Section 3 of the TO Tariff.
