Interconnection Request in the form of Attachment 1 to this LLIP for processing 
under the LLIP.  Consistent with Section 10A.2.1 of the TO Tariff, the Large 
Load Interconnection Customer shall send a copy of the Interconnection Request 
to the ISO, and the Interconnection Request and all supporting documentation 
shall be submitted electronically to the Participating TO in the manner posted on 
the Participating TO’s public website.   
 
An Interconnection Request for the expansion of capacity of an existing Large 
Load shall be treated the same as an Interconnection Request for a new Large 
Load pursuant to this LLIP.  
 
Co-located generation serving a Large Load that will not export to the ISO 
Controlled Grid shall be interconnected in accordance with the generator 
interconnection rules of the applicable ECLL, as approved by its Local 
Regulatory Authority (including, for a UDC subject to the jurisdiction of the 
CPUC, CPUC Electric Rule 21), consistent with Section 10A.5 of the TO Tariff; 
provided that, where such co-located generation is included in the Interconnection 
Request, the Participating TO will evaluate its incremental impacts on the 
Participating TO’s Transmission System as part of the LLIP study process. Co-
located generation that will export to the ISO Controlled Grid is required to 
submit a generator interconnection request to the ISO in accordance with Section 
25.7.6 of the ISO Tariff for evaluation of the proposed generator interconnection 
and the Large Load will be evaluated pursuant to the LLIP.  For a Large Load co-
located with an exporting generating facility, the ISO will be a party to a pro 
forma agreement that bridges the generator’s Large Generator Interconnection 
Agreement with the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, or will negotiate a 
non-conforming Large Generator Interconnection Agreement, consistent with 
Section 10A.5 of the TO Tariff. 
 
3.2 
Transmission Interconnection Service 
 
3.2.1 The Product.  Transmission Interconnection Service allows Large Load 
Interconnection Customer to connect the Large Load to the Participating

7 
 
TO’s Transmission System and be eligible to receive electric energy and 
capacity from the ISO Controlled Grid. 
 
3.2.2 No Applicability to Transmission Service.  Nothing in this LLIP shall 
constitute a request for transmission service or confer upon a Large Load 
Interconnection Customer any right to receive transmission service.   
 
3.2.3 Roles and Responsibilities. 
 
3.2.3.1 Each Interconnection Request will be subject to the direction and 
oversight of the Participating TO.  The Participating TO will 
conduct or cause to be performed the required Interconnection 
Studies and any additional studies the Participating TO determines 
to be reasonably necessary.  The analysis of impacts on, and 
upgrades required to, the Participating TO’s Transmission System 
will be performed by the Participating TO and will be subject to 
review and concurrence by the ISO.  The Participating TO will 
perform all required studies related to the Participating TO’s 
Transmission System and will coordinate with Affected System 
Operators in accordance with LLIP Section 3.5. 
 
3.2.3.2 The Participating TO will complete or cause to be completed all 
studies as required within the timelines provided in this LLIP. 
 
 
3.2.3.3 Each Large Load Interconnection Customer shall pay the actual 
costs of all Interconnection Studies, and any additional studies the 
Participating TO determines to be reasonably necessary in 
response to the Interconnection Request.  The Participating TO 
shall reimburse the ISO for the actual cost of any portion of the 
Interconnection Studies that the ISO performs related to the ISO 
Controlled Grid, as applicable.  
 
 
3.2.3.3.1 The Participating TO shall issue invoices for 
Interconnection Studies that shall include a detailed and 
itemized accounting of the cost of each Interconnection 
Study.  Whenever the actual cost of performing the 
Interconnection Studies exceeds the Interconnection 
Study Deposit, the Large Load Interconnection Customer 
shall pay the undisputed difference in accordance with the 
Participating TO issued invoice within thirty (30) 
Calendar Days.  The Participating TO shall not be 
obligated to continue to have any studies conducted 
unless the Large Load Interconnection Customer has paid 
all undisputed amounts in compliance herewith.

8 
 
3.3 
Comparability 
Participating TO shall receive, process and analyze all Interconnection Requests 
in a timely manner as set forth in this LLIP.  Participating TO will use the same 
Reasonable Efforts in processing and analyzing Interconnection Requests from all 
Large Load Interconnection Customers, whether the Large Load is owned by 
Participating TO and its Affiliates or by a third party.   
 
3.4 
Base Case Data 
Participating TO shall provide Base Case data to a Large Load Interconnection 
Customer upon request subject to confidentiality provisions in LLIP Section 7.1. 
Participating TO shall provide base power flow, short circuit databases, including 
all underlying assumptions, and contingency list used in the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer’s Interconnection Studies.  Participating TO is 
permitted to require that the Large Load Interconnection Customer sign a 
confidentiality agreement before the release of commercially sensitive 
information or Critical Energy Infrastructure Information in the Base Case data.  
Such Base Cases may include all (i) Large Loads, (ii) generation projects, and (iii) 
transmission projects, including merchant transmission projects that are proposed 
for the Participating TO’s Transmission System for which a transmission 
expansion plan has been submitted and approved by the applicable authority. 
 
 
3.5 
Coordination with Affected Systems 
The Participating TO will notify the Affected System Operators that are 
potentially affected by a Large Load Interconnection Customer’s Interconnection 
Request.  The Participating TO will coordinate the conduct of any studies 
required to determine the impact of the Interconnection Request on Affected 
Systems with Affected System Operators and, if possible, include those results (if 
available) in its applicable Interconnection Study within the time frame specified 
in this LLIP.  Participating TO will include such Affected System Operators in all 
meetings held with Large Load Interconnection Customer as required by this 
LLIP.  Large Load Interconnection Customer will cooperate with Participating 
TO in all matters related to the conduct of studies and the determination of 
modifications to Affected Systems.  If an Affected System Operator, that has been 
informed its system is an Affected System refuses to cooperate with the 
Participating TO with whom interconnection has been requested in all matters 
related to the conduct of studies and the determination of whether modifications 
to its Affected System are necessary to avoid adverse impacts, it waives any right 
in any fora that the Participating TO’s provision of service has adversely impacted 
such Affected System Operator. 
 
3.6 
Capacity of the Large Load  
 
The Interconnection Request shall be evaluated using the maximum capacity 
requested by the Large Load Interconnection Customer.  However, if the 
maximum capacity that the Large Load is capable of receiving is greater than the

9 
 
maximum capacity requested by the Large Load Interconnection Customer, the 
Large Load Interconnection Customer will be required to limit the Large Load 
capacity to no greater than the amount requested (e.g., through use of a control 
system, power relay(s), or other similar device settings or adjustments), and the 
Large Load Interconnection Customer must obtain the Participating TO’s 
agreement, with such agreement not to be unreasonably withheld, that the manner 
in which the Large Load Interconnection Customer proposes to implement such a 
limit will not adversely affect the safety and reliability of the Participating TO’s 
Transmission System.  If the Participating TO does not so agree, then the 
Interconnection Request must be withdrawn or revised to specify the maximum 
capacity that the Large Load is capable of receiving.    Furthermore, nothing in 
this section shall prevent a Participating TO from considering a capacity higher 
than the limited capacity, if appropriate, when evaluating system protection 
impacts. 
 
3.7 
Proposed Service Commencement Date 
The  proposed Service Commencement Date of the new Large Load or increase in 
capacity of the existing Large Load shall not exceed seven years from the date the 
Interconnection Request is received by Participating TO for those Interconnection 
Requests studied in accordance with the Large Load Interconnection Procedures, 
unless Large Load Interconnection Customer demonstrates and the Participating 
TO agrees, such agreement not to be unreasonably withheld, that engineering, 
permitting and construction of the new Large Load or increase in capacity of the 
existing Large Load will take longer than the seven-year period.    
 
3.7.1 Interconnection Request.  If the proposed Service Commencement Date in 
the Interconnection Request is more than seven years from the date the 
Interconnection Request is received by the Participating TO, the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer must demonstrate, subject to the Participating TO’s 
agreement, such agreement not to be unreasonably withheld, that the required 
engineering, permitting and construction of the Large Load will take longer than 
the seven-year period.  
 
3.7.2 After Start of the Large Load Interconnection Study.  Any request to 
extend the Service Commencement Date after commencement of the Large Load 
Interconnection Study under the LLIP, or following execution of a Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement, shall be subject to the following: 
 
(i) Requested extension does not exceed seven years from Service 
Commencement Date in the original Interconnection Request.  A request 
to extend the Service Commencement Date that does not exceed seven 
years from the Service Commencement Date in the original 
Interconnection Request is subject to the modification assessment process 
specified in LLIP Section 4.6.1.6.1.  
 
(ii) Requested extension exceeds seven years from Service Commencement 
Date in the original Interconnection Request.  A request to extend the

10 
 
Service Commencement Date that exceeds seven years from the Service 
Commencement Date in the original Interconnection Request shall (a) 
demonstrate, subject to the Participating TO’s agreement, such agreement 
not to be unreasonably withheld, that engineering, permitting and 
construction of the new Large Load or increase in capacity of the existing 
Large Load will take longer than the seven-year period, and (b) be subject 
to the modification assessment process specified in LLIP Section 
4.6.1.6.1. 
 
Any extension of the Service Commencement Date under this LLIP Section 3.7.2 
shall not extend the Outside Date under any applicable Cost Recovery Agreement 
unless the parties to that agreement agree in writing to such extension. 
 
3.8   Queue Position 
 
           3.8.1 Assignment of Queue Position. 
Participating TO shall assign a Queue Position as follows: the Queue 
Position shall be assigned based upon the date and time of receipt of all 
items required pursuant to the provisions of LLIP Section 4.2.1.   
 
3.8.2 Higher Queue Position.  
A higher Queue Position assigned to an Interconnection Request is one 
that has been placed “earlier” in the queue in relation to another 
Interconnection Request that is assigned a lower Queue Position.  
 
 
3.9 
Withdrawal 
Large Load Interconnection Customer may withdraw its Interconnection Request 
at any time by written notice of such withdrawal to Participating TO, and the 
Participating TO will notify the ISO and Affected System Operators, if any, 
within three (3) Business Days of receipt of such a notice.  In addition, after 
confirmation by the Participating TO of a valid Interconnection Request, if the 
Large Load Interconnection Customer fails to adhere to all requirements of this 
LLIP, except as provided in LLIP Section 7.2 (Disputes), Participating TO shall 
deem the Interconnection Request to be withdrawn and shall provide written 
notice to Large Load Interconnection Customer of the deemed withdrawal within 
five (5) Business Days and an explanation of the reasons for such deemed 
withdrawal.  Upon receipt of such written notice, Large Load Interconnection 
Customer shall have five (5) Business Days in which to either (i) respond with 
information or action that cures the deficiency, or (ii) support its position that the 
deemed withdrawal was erroneous and notify the Participating TO of its intent to 
pursue Dispute Resolution. 
 
For an Interconnection Request under the LLIP, withdrawal shall result in the 
removal of the Interconnection Request from the Interconnection Studies.  If a 
Large Load Interconnection Customer disputes the withdrawal and removal from 
the Interconnection Studies and has elected to pursue Dispute Resolution, Large

11 
 
Load Interconnection Customer's Interconnection Request will not be considered 
in any ongoing Interconnection Study during the Dispute Resolution process. 
 
In the event of such withdrawal, Participating TO, subject to the provisions in 
LLIP Section 7.1, as applicable, shall provide, at Large Load Interconnection 
Customer's request, all information that Participating TO developed for any 
completed study conducted up to the date of withdrawal of the Interconnection 
Request. 
 
3.10 
Withdrawal Penalty 
 
A Large Load Interconnection Customer with an Interconnection Request being 
processed under the LLIP will be subject to a Withdrawal Penalty if it withdraws 
its Interconnection Request or is deemed withdrawn, or the Large Load does not 
otherwise achieve its Service Commencement Date, which date may be modified 
if the necessary Participating TO-owned facilities cannot be constructed on a 
timeline that meets such date, unless: (1) the withdrawal does not have a material 
impact on the cost or timing of any equal or later queued interconnection request; 
(2) Large Load Interconnection Customer withdraws after receiving Large Load 
Interconnection Customer’s most recent Interconnection Study report and the 
Large Load Network Upgrade costs assigned to the Interconnection Request 
identified in that report have increased by more than twenty-five percent (25%) 
compared to costs identified in Large Load Interconnection Customer’s preceding 
Interconnection Study report; or (3) Large Load Interconnection Customer 
withdraws after receiving an Interconnection Study report issued after completion 
of the initial Large Load Interconnection Study and the Large Load Network 
Upgrade costs assigned to the Interconnection Request identified in such 
Interconnection Study report have increased by more than one hundred percent 
(100%) compared to costs identified in the initial Large Load Interconnection 
Study report. 
 
3.10.1 Calculation of the Withdrawal Penalty 
 
If the Large Load Interconnection Customer withdraws its Interconnection 
Request or is deemed withdrawn prior to the commencement of the Large 
Load Interconnection Study, Large Load Interconnection Customer will 
not be subject to a Withdrawal Penalty.  If Large Load Interconnection 
Customer withdraws, is deemed withdrawn, or otherwise does not achieve 
its Service Commencement Date at any point after the commencement of 
the Large Load Interconnection Study, that Large Load Interconnection 
Customer’s Withdrawal Penalty will be the greater of: (1) the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer’s Interconnection Study Deposit required under 
LLIP Section 4.2.1; or (2) as follows in (a)–(c): 
 
(a) If Large Load Interconnection Customer withdraws or is deemed

12 
 
withdrawn during the Large Load Interconnection Study or after 
receipt of a Large Load Interconnection Study report, Large Load 
Interconnection Customer will be charged two (2) times the actual cost 
of the Large Load Interconnection Study performed for the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer. 
 
(b) If Large Load Interconnection Customer withdraws or is deemed 
withdrawn after receipt of the draft Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement but before Large Load Interconnection Customer has 
executed a Large Load Interconnection Agreement or has requested 
that its Large Load Interconnection Agreement be filed unexecuted, 
Large Load Interconnection Customer will be charged ten percent 
(10%) of its estimated Large Load Network Upgrade costs as reflected 
in the most recently completed Interconnection Study.   
 
(c) If Large Load Interconnection Customer has executed a Large 
Load Interconnection Agreement or has requested that its Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement be filed unexecuted and subsequently 
withdraws its Interconnection Request, the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer’s Withdrawal Penalty will be calculated as set forth in the 
Large Load Interconnection Agreement.   
 
The Commercial Readiness Deposit shall be retained as financial security 
for the Withdrawal Penalty (if applicable) and, other than as set forth in 
the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, any security not applied to the 
Withdrawal Penalty will be released to the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer following withdrawal or the Service Commencement Date.  
Where a Cost Recovery Agreement applies, (i) any Commercial Readiness 
Deposit or Interconnection Financial Security provided for the same costs 
shall count toward, and shall not be duplicated by, the Construction 
Security required under the Cost Recovery Agreement, and (ii) any 
Withdrawal Penalty paid with respect to a Large Load Network Upgrade 
shall be credited against the Pre-In-Service Termination Costs payable 
under the Cost Recovery Agreement for that upgrade, so that the 
Participating TO does not recover the same costs more than once. 
 
3.11 
Standards for Co-located Inverter Based Generating Facilities 
 
Inverters used for the production, and/or later injection from storage, of electricity 
shall meet the inverter certification standards of UL-1741 and UL-1741 
Supplement B. 
 
Section 4.  Large Load Study Process 
 
4.1 
Timing For Submitting Interconnection Requests 
A Large Load Interconnection Customer may submit an Interconnection Request 
for processing under the LLIP at any time during the year. The Participating TO,

13 
 
in coordination with the ISO, as applicable, will study the Interconnection 
Request.   
 
4.2 
Processing of Interconnection Request 
 
4.2.1 
Initiating an Interconnection Request.  To initiate an 
Interconnection Request under the LLIP, Large Load Interconnection 
Customer must submit all of the following: (i) an Interconnection Study 
Deposit of $250,000; (ii) a completed Interconnection Request in the form 
of Attachment 1 to the LLIP, including preferred Point of Interconnection 
and voltage level, all information required by Section 10A.2.1 of the TO 
Tariff (other than any election of interim service, which shall be made in 
accordance with LLIP Section 4.6.2), and all other technical data; (iii) a 
Commercial Readiness Deposit equal to two times the Interconnection 
Study Deposit described in this LLIP Section 4.2.1 in the form of an 
irrevocable letter of credit, cash, a surety bond, or other form of security 
that is reasonably acceptable to Participating TO, in accordance with LLIP 
Section 4.7.1. This Commercial Readiness Deposit is refunded to Large 
Load Interconnection Customer according to LLIP Section 3.10.1; 
however, the Participating TO shall be entitled to hold the Commercial 
Readiness Deposit until the Large Load Interconnection Customer’s Large 
Load achieves its Service Commencement Date; and (iv) demonstration of 
Site Control.   
 
4.2.1.1 Use of Interconnection Study Deposit.  The Interconnection 
Study Deposit shall be applied to pay for prudent costs incurred by 
the Participating TO, the ISO, or third parties at the direction of the 
Participating TO or ISO, as applicable, to perform and administer 
the Interconnection Studies.   
 
In the event a Large Load Interconnection Customer withdraws its 
Interconnection Request prior to the commencement of the Large 
Load Interconnection Study, Large Load Interconnection Customer 
must pay Participating TO the actual costs of processing its 
Interconnection Request. In the event a Large Load 
Interconnection Customer withdraws after commencement of the 
Large Load Interconnection Study, Participating TO shall charge 
and Large Load Interconnection Customer shall pay the actual 
costs of the Interconnection Studies.  
 
Any difference between the Interconnection Study Deposit and the 
actual cost of the Interconnection Studies shall be paid by or 
refunded to the Large Load Interconnection Customer. Any 
invoices for Interconnection Studies shall include a detailed and 
itemized accounting of the cost of each Interconnection Study. 
Large Load Interconnection Customers shall pay any such 
undisputed costs within thirty (30) Calendar Days of receipt of an

14 
 
invoice. If Large Load Interconnection Customer fails to pay such 
undisputed costs within the time allotted, its Interconnection 
Request shall be deemed withdrawn and will be subject to a 
Withdrawal Penalty pursuant to LLIP Section 3.10.1. 
 
The Participating TO will reimburse the ISO or third parties, as 
applicable, for all work performed on behalf of the withdrawn 
Interconnection Request at the Participating TO’s direction. The 
Large Load Interconnection Customer must pay all monies due 
before it is allowed to obtain any Interconnection Study data or 
results. 
 
 
4.3 
Validation of Interconnection Request 
 
4.3.1 Acknowledgment of Interconnection Request.  Participating TO shall 
notify the Large Load Interconnection Customer within ten (10) Business 
Days of receipt of the Interconnection Request, which notice shall state 
whether the Interconnection Request is deemed valid.   
 
4.3.2 Deficiencies in Interconnection Request.  An Interconnection Request 
will not be considered to be a valid request until all items in LLIP Section 
4.2.1 have been received by Participating TO and deemed valid by the 
Participating TO.  If an Interconnection Request fails to meet the 
requirements set forth in LLIP Section 4.2.1, Participating TO shall 
include in its notification to the Large Load Interconnection Customer 
under LLIP Section 4.3.1 the reasons for such failure and that the 
Interconnection Request does not constitute a valid request.  Consistent 
with Section 10A.2.3 of the TO Tariff, the Participating TO will attempt to 
remedy deficiencies in the Interconnection Request through informal 
communications with the Large Load Interconnection Customer, and the 
Large Load Interconnection Customer shall provide Participating TO the 
additional requested information needed to constitute a valid request.  
Whenever the additional requested information is provided by the Large 
Load Interconnection Customer, the Participating TO shall notify the 
Large Load Interconnection Customer within five (5) Business Days of 
receipt of the additional requested information whether the 
Interconnection Request is valid.  If the Interconnection Request continues 
to fail to meet the requirements set forth in LLIP Section 4.2.1, the 
Participating TO shall include in its notification to the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer the reasons for such failure.  If an 
Interconnection Request has not been deemed valid, the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer must submit all information necessary to meet 
the requirements of LLIP Section 4.2.1 no later than twenty (20) Business 
Days after the date the original Interconnection Request was submitted, or 
ten (10) Business Days after the Participating TO first provided notice that 
the Interconnection Request was not valid, whichever is later.

15 
 
Interconnection Requests that have not met the requirements of LLIP 
Section 4.2.1 within twenty (20) Business Days after the date the original 
Interconnection Request was submitted or ten (10) Business Days after the 
Participating TO first provided notice that the Interconnection Request 
was not valid, whichever is later, will be deemed invalid, will be returned 
to the Large Load Interconnection Customer in accordance with Section 
10A.2.3 of the TO Tariff, and will not be included in the LLIP.  
 
Interconnection Requests deemed invalid under this LLIP Section 4.3.2 
are not subject to LLIP Section 3.9.  Large Load Interconnection 
Customers with invalid Interconnection Requests under this LLIP Section 
4.3.2 may seek relief under LLIP Section 7.2 by so notifying the 
Participating TO within two (2) Business Days of the notice of invalidity. 
 
4.4     Potential Deferral of the Interconnection Studies 
 
           The Participating TO may defer commencement of the Large Load 
Interconnection Study when it determines, using Good Utility Practice and 
reasonable engineering judgment, that the Interconnection Request cannot be 
studied meaningfully until other pending study results for higher-queued projects 
are available. 
 
           Within ten (10) Business Days after deeming an Interconnection Request valid 
under LLIP Section 4.3.1, the Participating TO will notify the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer in writing if it is deferring the start of the 
Interconnection Studies. The notice will include: (i) information regarding the 
pending studies; and (ii) the estimated start date of the Large Load 
Interconnection Study.  During the period of deferral, the Participating TO will 
provide a monthly status update to the Large Load Interconnection Customer. 
 
 
4.5 
Scoping Meeting 
Within fifteen (15) Business Days after the Participating TO notifies the Large 
Load Interconnection Customer that the Interconnection Request has been 
deemed valid as set forth in LLIP Section 4.3.2, the Participating TO shall 
establish a date agreeable to the Large Load Interconnection Customer, and the 
ISO, if applicable, for the Scoping Meeting.   
 
The purpose of the Scoping Meeting shall be to discuss reasonable Service 
Commencement Dates and alternative interconnection options, to exchange 
information including any transmission data that would reasonably be expected to 
impact such interconnection options, to analyze such information and to 
determine the potential feasible Points of Interconnection and eliminate 
alternatives given resources and available information. The Scoping Meeting shall 
also include discussion of a deferral of the Interconnection Studies in accordance 
with LLIP Section 4.4.

16 
 
The Participating TO will bring to the meeting, as reasonably necessary to 
accomplish its purpose, such already available technical data, including, but not 
limited to, (i) general facility loadings, (ii) general instability issues, (iii) general 
short circuit issues, (iv) general voltage issues, and (v) general reliability issues.    
 
The Large Load Interconnection Customer will bring to the Scoping Meeting, in 
addition to the technical data form (Appendix A to Attachment 1) submitted with 
its Interconnection Request, any system studies previously performed.  The 
Participating TO, the ISO, if applicable, and the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer will also bring to the meeting personnel and other resources as may be 
reasonably required to accomplish the purpose of the meeting in the time 
allocated for the meeting.  On the basis of the meeting, the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer shall designate its Point of Interconnection.  The 
duration of the meeting shall be sufficient to accomplish its purpose. 
 
Within five (5) Business Days after the Scoping Meeting, the Participating TO  
shall tender to the Large Load Interconnection Customer a Large Load Study 
Process Agreement developed by the Participating TO consistent with the TO 
Tariff and this LLIP, which shall contain an outline of the scope of the Large 
Load Interconnection Study, contain a non-binding good faith estimate of the cost 
to perform such study, and shall specify that the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer is responsible for the actual cost of the Interconnection Studies, 
including reasonable administrative costs.  No later than thirty (30) Calendar Days 
after the Scoping Meeting, the Large Load Interconnection Customer shall either 
execute and deliver to the Participating TO  the Large Load Study Process 
Agreement or request that the Participating TO file it unexecuted with FERC, or 
the Interconnection Request shall be deemed withdrawn.  If an unexecuted filing 
is requested, the Interconnection Studies will be paused until the Large Load 
Study Process Agreement is made effective by FERC. 
 
4.6 
Interconnection Studies 
The Interconnection Studies shall consist of a Large Load Interconnection Study, 
any FILI Study requested pursuant to LLIP Section 4.6.2, and any additional 
studies, including but not limited to those identified in LLIP Section 4.6.3 
required for interconnection of the Large Load, and co-located generation not 
exporting to the ISO Controlled Grid, to the Participating TO’s Transmission 
System.    The analysis of impacts on, and upgrades required to, the Participating 
TO’s Transmission System will be performed by the Participating TO and will be 
subject to the review and concurrence of the ISO in accordance with Section 25.7 
of the ISO Tariff. The Interconnection Studies will identify Participating TO’s 
Interconnection Facilities and required Large Load Network Upgrades necessary 
to mitigate thermal overloads and voltage violations, and address short circuit, 
stability, and reliability issues associated with the requested Transmission 
Interconnection Service.

17 
 
All cost estimates for Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities and Large 
Load Network Upgrades, as applicable, contained in the Interconnection Studies 
will be set forth in the Interconnection Study report in present dollar costs as well 
as time-adjusted dollar costs, adjusted to the estimated year of construction of the 
components being constructed.   
 
The Participating TO will prepare an Interconnection Study report to document 
the results of the Interconnection Studies.   
 
4.6.1 Large Load Interconnection Study.  
 
 
4.6.1.1  Scope of the Large Load Interconnection Study.  The Large 
Load Interconnection Study will consist of a  short circuit analysis, 
a power flow analysis, an electromagnetic transient (“EMT”) 
screening, a non-binding good faith estimate of the scope and cost 
of the Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities and Large Load 
Network Upgrades, and any other studies that are deemed 
necessary. The Large Load Interconnection Study will also identify 
the need for any additional studies (e.g., stability analysis, EMT 
study, etc.) to be performed as part of the scope of work set forth in 
the Large Load Interconnection Agreement pursuant to LLIP 
Section 4.6.3.  When there is co-located generation not exporting 
to the ISO Controlled Grid and not subject to electrical short 
circuit duty dependence, the Large Load Interconnection Study 
will identify the impacts associated with the Large Load and any 
incremental impacts of the co-located generation.       
The Large Load Interconnection Study will consider the use of 
alternative transmission technologies including dynamic line 
ratings, advanced power flow control devices, advanced 
conductors, and transmission switching, when evaluating 
transmission solutions to accommodate new Large Loads and their 
associated transmission system impacts.  If traditional network 
upgrades are selected instead of alternative transmission 
technologies, the Participating TO will provide a demonstration of 
why alternative transmission technologies are not feasible or would 
not result in lower costs or a faster timeline for accommodating the 
interconnection of the Large Load.  
The Large Load Interconnection Study shall state the assumptions 
upon which it is based, state the results of the analyses, and 
provide the requirement or potential impediments to providing the 
requested Transmission Interconnection Service, including an 
estimate of the cost and length of time that would be necessary to 
correct any problems identified in those analyses and implement 
the Interconnection.

18 
 
The Large Load Interconnection Study shall provide a list of 
Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities and Large Load 
Network Upgrades, as applicable, that are required as a result of 
the Interconnection Request. 
 
4.6.1.2 Timing of the Large Load Interconnection Study Results.  The 
Participating TO shall use Reasonable Efforts to complete the 
Large Load Interconnection Study within ninety (90) Calendar 
Days after the execution of a Large Load Study Process Agreement 
or, if the Large Load Study Process Agreement is filed unexecuted, 
after it is made effective by FERC.  The Participating TO will 
issue a Large Load Interconnection Study report to the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer. The Participating TO will share study 
results with the ISO for review and concurrence.   
 
At any time the Participating TO determines that it will not meet 
the required time frame for completing the Large Load 
Interconnection  Study, Participating TO shall notify the Large 
Load Interconnection Customer as to the schedule status of the 
Large Load Interconnection Study and provide an estimated 
completion date with an explanation of the reasons why additional 
time is required. 
 
Upon request, the Participating TO shall provide the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer all supporting documentation, 
workpapers and relevant pre-Interconnection Request and post-
Interconnection Request power flow and short circuit databases for 
the Large Load Interconnection Study, subject to confidentiality 
arrangements consistent with LLIP Section 7.1. 
 
Should the Large Load Interconnection Customer provide written 
comments on the Large Load Interconnection Study report at least 
five (5) Business Days before the Report Meeting conducted to 
discuss the report, the Participating TO will address the written 
comments in the Large Load Interconnection Study Report 
Meeting.  Should the Large Load Interconnection Customer 
provide comments at any later time (up to the time of the Report 
Meeting), then such comments shall be considered informal 
inquiries to which the Participating TO will provide informal, 
informational responses at the Report Meeting, to the extent 
possible.  
 
The Large Load Interconnection Customer may submit, in writing, 
additional comments on the final Large Load Interconnection 
Study report up to three (3) Business Days following the Report 
Meeting.  Based on any discussion at the Report Meeting and any 
comments received from the Large Load Interconnection Customer

19 
 
or the ISO, the Participating TO will determine whether it is 
necessary to follow the Large Load Interconnection Study report 
with a revised study report.  The Participating TO will issue any 
such revised report to the Large Load Interconnection Customer no 
later than fifteen (15) Business Days following the Report 
Meeting. If the ISO has not completed its review of the Large Load 
Interconnection Study report, the Participating TO shall delay its 
determination of whether a revised study report is required until 
that review is complete. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
4.6.1.3 Large Load Interconnection Study Report Meeting.  A Report 
Meeting shall be held among the Participating TO, the ISO, if 
applicable, and the Large Load Interconnection Customer to 
discuss the results of the Large Load Interconnection Study, 
including assigned cost responsibility.  Any such Report Meeting 
will be held within ten (10) Business Days of the date the Large 
Load Interconnection Study report is provided to the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer.  
 
4.6.1.4 Commercial Readiness Deposit.  Within thirty (30) Calendar 
Days after receiving the final Large Load Interconnection Study 
report, the Large Load Interconnection Customer shall provide an 
additional Commercial Readiness Deposit sufficient to bring the 
aggregate Commercial Readiness Deposit to twenty percent (20%) 
of the Participating TO’s then-current estimated construction cost 
of the Large Load Network Upgrades identified in that report that 
are attributable to the Interconnection Request.  If the final Large 
Load Interconnection Study report is revised following ISO 
review, the required Commercial Readiness Deposit shall be 
adjusted to reflect twenty percent (20%) of the corresponding 
estimated construction cost identified in the revised final report, 
and any required increase shall be provided within thirty (30) 
Calendar Days after issuance of that report.  
 
 
The Commercial Readiness Deposit secures the Withdrawal 
Penalty and other pre-in-service obligations under this LLIP and 
the Large Load Interconnection Agreement. It does not establish a 
direct assignment of the Large Load Network Upgrade costs, 
constitute a payment toward an Annual MTRC, reduce the Total 
Required Revenue Commitment, or satisfy Operational Security 
under a Cost Recovery Agreement.

20 
 
To the extent a Commercial Readiness Deposit is in a form 
permitted under Schedule 3 of an applicable Cost Recovery 
Agreement, LS Power Grid may elect in writing to credit it dollar-
for-dollar toward required Construction Security under that 
agreement. No amount of Commercial Readiness Deposit may be 
applied or credited more than once. Any portion not so credited 
shall be administered and released under Sections 3.9 and 3.10 of 
this LLIP and the Large Load Interconnection Agreement. 
   
4.6.1.5 Restudy. If restudy of the Large Load Interconnection Study is 
required due to a higher queued project dropping out of the queue, 
or a modification of a higher queued project subject to LLIP 
Section 4.6.1.6, Participating TO shall notify Large Load 
Interconnection Customer in writing. Such restudy shall take no 
longer than forty-five (45) Calendar Days from the date of notice. 
Any cost of restudy shall be borne by the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer. 
 
4.6.1.6 Modifications.  At any time during the course of the 
Interconnection Studies, the Large Load Interconnection Customer, 
the Participating TO, or the ISO, as applicable, may identify 
changes to the planned interconnection that may improve the costs 
and benefits (including reliability) of the interconnection, and the 
ability of the proposed change to accommodate the Interconnection 
Request.  To the extent the identified changes are acceptable to the 
Participating TO, the ISO, as applicable, and Large Load 
Interconnection Customer, such acceptance not to be unreasonably 
withheld, Participating TO shall modify the configuration in 
accordance with such changes without altering the Interconnection 
Request’s eligibility for participating in Interconnection Studies.          
 
4.6.1.6.1 For any modifications other than those agreed upon under 
LLIP Section 4.6.1.6, the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer must first request that Participating TO evaluate 
whether such modification is a Material Modification.  In 
response to Large Load Interconnection Customer's 
request, Participating TO, in coordination with the ISO, if 
applicable, shall evaluate the proposed modifications prior 
to making them and inform Large Load Interconnection 
Customer in writing of whether the modifications would 
constitute a Material Modification.  The Participating TO 
may, at its option, engage the services of the ISO to assist 
in the assessment of the modification.  Any change to the 
Point of Interconnection shall constitute a Material 
Modification.

21 
 
 
The Large Load Interconnection Customer shall provide 
the Participating TO a $30,000 deposit for the modification 
assessment at the time the request is submitted.  Except as 
provided below, any modification assessment will be 
concluded, and a response provided to the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer in writing, within forty-five (45) 
Calendar Days from the date the Participating TO receives 
all of the following: 1) the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer’s written notice to modify the project; 2) a 
narrative description of the requested modification; 3) 
technical data required to assess the request, including an 
updated technical data form (Appendix A to Attachment 1 
to this LLIP), if requested by the Participating TO; 4) any 
additional information requested by Participating TO; and 
5) payment of the $30,000 deposit.  If applicable, the 
Participating TO shall coordinate the modification request 
with the ISO.  If the modification assessment cannot be 
completed within that time period, the Participating TO 
shall notify the Large Load Interconnection Customer and 
provide an estimated completion date with an explanation 
of the reasons why additional time is required.  The Large 
Load Interconnection Customer will be responsible for the 
actual costs incurred by the Participating TO and, if 
applicable, the ISO in conducting the modification 
assessment.  If the actual costs of the modification 
assessment are less than the deposit provided by the Large 
Load Interconnection Customer, the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer will be refunded the balance 
within thirty (30) Calendar Days of being invoiced.  If the 
actual costs of the modification assessment are greater than 
the deposit provided by the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer, the Large Load Interconnection Customer shall 
pay the balance within thirty (30) Calendar Days of being 
invoiced. 
 
If the proposed modification is determined to be a Material 
Modification by the Participating TO pursuant to the 
modification assessment described above, the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer shall then either:  
 
(i) 
withdraw the proposed modification, or  
 
(ii) withdraw the proposed modification and submit a 
new Interconnection Request reflecting such 
modification.

22 
 
4.6.2   Optional Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI) Study and 
Agreement. If the Large Load Interconnection Study finds that the full 
amount of the Interconnection Request cannot be accommodated prior to 
the time that all ECLL Interconnection Facilities are in service, the Large 
Load Interconnection Customer may request a FILI Study, by written 
notice to the Participating TO within thirty (30) Calendar Days after 
receipt of the final Large Load Interconnection Study report, to 
determine, consistent with Section 10A.4 of the TO Tariff, whether 
Interim Firm Interconnection Service and/or FILI Service may be 
provided.  A Large Load Interconnection Customer may elect to be 
studied only for Interim Firm Interconnection Service and not FILI 
Service.  If the Large Load Interconnection Customer elects to proceed 
with a FILI Study, the Participating TO shall use Reasonable Efforts to 
complete the FILI Study within sixty (60) Calendar Days after receipt of 
such request. Large Load Interconnection Customer will be responsible 
for the actual costs of the FILI Study. The Participating TO will perform 
the FILI Study. At any time the Participating TO determines that it will 
not meet the required time frame for completing the FILI Study, 
Participating TO shall notify the Large Load Interconnection Customer as 
to the schedule status of the FILI Study and provide an estimated 
completion date with an explanation of the reasons why additional time is 
required. 
 
 
 
 The FILI Study will determine (i) the maximum amount of Interim Firm 
Interconnection Service, if any, that can be provided prior to completion 
of the Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities and Large Load 
Network Upgrades; (ii) whether the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer is eligible to receive FILI Service and the maximum amount of 
such service; (iii) the conditions and limitations of such service; (iv) the 
upgrades and the associated cost; and (v) the estimated duration required 
to provide the interim service. The Participating TO will share study 
results with the ISO for review and concurrence.  The Participating TO 
shall update its analysis of the availability of FILI Service at least 
annually under the terms of the FILI Service Agreement, and the actual 
amount of FILI Service available during any operating period shall be 
determined by the Participating TO through operational assessments 
conducted closer to real-time operating conditions, consistent with 
Section 10A.4 of the TO Tariff.  If requested by the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer within ten (10) Business Days of the date of 
the issuance of the FILI Study report, a Report Meeting shall be 
scheduled among the Participating TO, the ISO, and the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer. 
 
 
 
The Large Load Interconnection Customer should note the following 
considerations: 
a) 
Temporary limits may be adjusted if unforeseen conditions arise. 
b) 
Advance notice of non-firm load curtailment may not be possible.

23 
 
c) 
Non-firm load may be curtailed during planned or repair outages, 
which may last longer than 6 months. 
d) 
ISO may have additional operational requirements. 
e) 
Participating TO is not obligated to provide flexibility beyond 
what it can, in its sole judgment, manage operationally. 
f) 
Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities costs for interim 
interconnection service will be directly assigned to the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer. 
g) 
Large Load Interconnection Customers not adhering to the 
contractual agreement and conditions may be curtailed indefinitely.  
 
4.6.2.1 FILI Service Agreement. If the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer has elected FILI Service, as reflected in the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement, the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer shall ensure that, prior to the Service Commencement 
Date, the Large Load Customer executes, or requests to be filed 
unexecuted with FERC, a FILI Service Agreement with the 
Participating TO and, as applicable, the ISO, developed by the 
Participating TO consistent with Section 10A.4 of the TO Tariff 
and in accordance with ISO Tariff Section 25.7.2. The FILI 
Service Agreement shall describe the circumstances in which the 
ISO or Participating TO may temporarily curtail the Large Load 
receiving FILI Service, and the mechanism the ISO or 
Participating TO will use to perform the curtailment. The ISO will 
post such FILI Service Agreements on the ISO Website.  
 
4.6.3   Additional Studies. The Participating TO may identify the need for 
additional studies to comply with Applicable Reliability Standards. These 
additional studies may include, but are not limited to, the following: 
stability analysis, variable load impact analysis, and EMT analysis.  The 
associated new scope will be identified in the Large Load Interconnection 
Study pursuant to LLIP Section 4.6.1.1. The additional studies will be 
performed by the Participating TO as part of the scope of work set forth in 
the Large Load Interconnection Agreement. The additional studies may 
result in the identification of additional facilities scope and cost, and may 
require a revision to the schedule set forth in the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement. The Large Load Interconnection Customer 
will be responsible for providing the necessary technical information 
and/or models requested by the Participating TO to conduct the additional 
studies. The Large Load Interconnection Customer will be responsible for 
the costs of such studies.            
 
If an additional study results in the need to revise the scope of work of the 
Large Load Network Upgrades identified in the Large Load 
Interconnection Study and the updated assigned costs have increased by 
more than twenty-five percent (25%) compared to costs identified in the 
Large Load Interconnection Study report, the Large Load Interconnection

24 
 
Customer shall not be subject to a Withdrawal Penalty under LLIP Section 
3.10.1 if the Interconnection Request is withdrawn within thirty (30) 
Calendar Days of receipt of the additional study report.  If the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer elects to continue with its Interconnection 
Request, the Large Load Interconnection Agreement will be amended to 
reflect the results of the additional study. 
 
4.6.4   Financing of Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities and Large 
Load Network Upgrades.  The responsibility to finance Participating 
TO’s Interconnection Facilities shall be assigned solely to the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer. The Participating TO will be responsible for 
financing Large Load Network Upgrades in accordance with the Large 
Load Interconnection Agreement and, as to any Large Load Network 
Upgrades that constitute Large Load-Driven Upgrades, the Cost Recovery 
Agreement required under LLIP Section 5.3.   
 
4.7 
Interconnection Financial Security   
 
4.7.1 Types of Interconnection Financial Security.  The Interconnection 
Financial Security posted by a Large Load Interconnection Customer may 
be any combination of the following types of Interconnection Financial 
Security provided in favor of the Participating TO: 
 
(a) 
an irrevocable and unconditional letter of credit issued by a bank 
or financial institution that has a credit rating of A or better by 
Standard and Poor’s or A2 or better by Moody’s;  
 
(b) 
an irrevocable and unconditional surety bond issued by an 
insurance company that has a credit rating of A or better by 
Standard and Poor’s or A2 or better by Moody’s; 
 
(c) 
an unconditional and irrevocable guaranty issued by a company 
that has a credit rating of A or better by Standard and Poor’s or A2 
or better by Moody’s; 
 
(d) 
a cash deposit standing to the credit of the Participating TO and in 
an interest-bearing escrow account maintained at a bank or 
financial institution that is reasonably acceptable to the 
Participating TO; 
 
(e) 
a certificate of deposit in the name of the Participating TO issued 
by a bank or financial institution that has a credit rating of A or 
better by Standard and Poor’s or A2 or better by Moody’s; or  
 
(f) 
a payment bond certificate in the name of the Participating TO 
issued by a bank or financial institution that has a credit rating of A 
or better by Standard and Poor’s or A2 or better by Moody’s.

25 
 
 
Interconnection Financial Security instruments as listed above shall be in 
such form as the Participating TO may reasonably require from time to 
time by notice to Large Load Interconnection Customers, or in such other 
form as has been evaluated and approved as reasonably acceptable by the 
Participating TO.     
 
The Participating TO shall require the use of standardized forms of 
Interconnection Financial Security to the greatest extent possible.  If at any 
time the guarantor of the Interconnection Financial Security fails to 
maintain the credit rating required by this LLIP Section 4.7.1, the Large 
Load Interconnection Customer shall provide to the Participating TO 
replacement Interconnection Financial Security meeting the requirements 
of this LLIP Section 4.7.1 within five (5) Business Days of the change in 
credit rating.  
 
Interest on a cash deposit standing to the credit of the Participating TO in 
an interest-bearing escrow account under subpart (d) of this LLIP Section 
4.7.1 will accrue to the Large Load Interconnection Customer’s benefit.  
 
Execution and filing of the Large Load Interconnection Agreement at 
FERC are addressed in LLIP Section 5. 
 
Section 5. 
Large Load Interconnection Agreement  
 
5.1 
Tender.  Within thirty (30) Calendar Days after the Report Meeting for the final Large 
Load Interconnection Study report or, if the Large Load Interconnection 
Customer has timely requested a FILI Study pursuant to LLIP Section 4.6.2, 
within thirty (30) Calendar Days after issuance of the final FILI Study report (or, 
if a Report Meeting is requested for the FILI Study, after such Report Meeting), 
the Participating TO shall tender to the Large Load Interconnection Customer a 
draft Large Load Interconnection Agreement developed by the Participating TO 
consistent with the TO Tariff, this LLIP, and the results of the Interconnection 
Studies.  The draft Large Load Interconnection Agreement shall address, without 
limitation, the scope, schedule, cost responsibility, payment provisions, cost 
recovery, and financial security for the Participating TO’s Interconnection 
Facilities and Large Load Network Upgrades, and any applicable operating 
requirements.  The Large Load Interconnection Customer shall provide written 
comments, or notification of no comments, on the draft Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement within thirty (30) Calendar Days. 
 
5.2 
Negotiation.  Notwithstanding LLIP Section 5.1, at the request of Large Load 
Interconnection Customer, Participating TO shall begin negotiations with Large 
Load Interconnection Customer concerning the terms and conditions of the Large 
Load Interconnection Agreement at any time after the Participating TO provides 
the Large Load Interconnection Customer with the final Large Load 
Interconnection Study report, or the final FILI Study report, if applicable.

26 
 
Participating TO and Large Load Interconnection Customer shall negotiate in 
good faith concerning any disputed provisions of the draft Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement for not more than sixty (60) Calendar Days after the 
Participating TO provides the Large Load Interconnection Customer with the final 
Large Load Interconnection Study report or the final FILI Study report if 
applicable.  If Large Load Interconnection Customer determines that negotiations 
are at an impasse, it may request termination of the negotiations at any time after 
tender of the draft Large Load Interconnection Agreement pursuant to LLIP 
Section 5.1 and request submission of the unexecuted Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement with FERC or initiate Dispute Resolution procedures pursuant to LLIP 
Section 7.2.  If Large Load Interconnection Customer requests termination of the 
negotiations, but within sixty (60) Calendar Days after issuance of the final Large 
Load Interconnection Study report, or the final FILI Study report if applicable, 
fails to request either the filing of the unexecuted Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement or initiate Dispute Resolution, it shall be deemed to have withdrawn 
its Interconnection Request.  Unless otherwise agreed by the Parties, if Large 
Load Interconnection Customer has not executed the Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement, requested filing of an unexecuted Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement, or initiated Dispute Resolution procedures pursuant to LLIP Section 
7.2 within the time period set forth in LLIP Section 5.3, it shall be deemed to have 
withdrawn its Interconnection Request.  Participating TO shall provide to Large 
Load Interconnection Customer a final Large Load Interconnection Agreement 
within fifteen (15) Business Days after the completion of the negotiation process. 
 
 
The Participating TO may declare an impasse upon sixty (60) Calendar Days after 
issuance of the final Large Load Interconnection Study report, or the final FILI 
Study report if applicable, or at any time following sixty (60) Calendar Days after 
issuance of the final Large Load Interconnection Study report, or the final FILI 
Study report if applicable, if the Parties have agreed to extend negotiation of the 
Large Load Interconnection Agreement.  If the Participating TO declares an 
impasse, the Participating TO will file the Large Load Interconnection Agreement 
unexecuted with FERC within twenty-one (21) Calendar Days. 
 
5.3 
Execution and Filing 
Within thirty (30) Business Days after receipt of the final Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement, Large Load Interconnection Customer shall either: (i) 
execute the final Large Load Interconnection Agreement and return it to 
Participating TO; or (ii) request in writing that Participating TO file with FERC 
the Large Load Interconnection Agreement in unexecuted form, or its 
Interconnection Request shall be deemed withdrawn and subject to LLIP Section 
3.10.  To the extent FERC filing is required, as soon as practicable, but not later 
than ten (10) Business Days after receiving either the executed Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement or the request to file an unexecuted Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement, Participating TO shall file the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement with FERC, together with, in the case of an 
unexecuted Large Load Interconnection Agreement, its explanation of any matters 
as to which Large Load Interconnection Customer and Participating TO disagree

27 
 
and support for the costs that Participating TO proposes to charge to Large Load 
Interconnection Customer under the Large Load Interconnection Agreement.  An 
unexecuted Large Load Interconnection Agreement should contain terms and 
conditions deemed appropriate by Participating TO for the Interconnection 
Request.  If the Parties agree to proceed with design, procurement, and 
construction of facilities and upgrades under the agreed-upon terms of the 
unexecuted Large Load Interconnection Agreement, they may proceed pending 
FERC action.  As a condition to the Participating TO’s design, procurement, 
construction, or operation of any Large Load-Driven Upgrades (as defined in the 
pro forma Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement set forth in Appendix V to the 
TO Tariff) associated with the Interconnection Request, the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer shall also, within the same period and subject to the 
same consequences as the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, execute and 
maintain a Cost Recovery Agreement substantially in the form set forth in 
Appendix V to the TO Tariff, or, if the Large Load Interconnection Customer 
requests that the Cost Recovery Agreement be filed unexecuted with FERC, 
comply with that agreement as made effective by FERC.  A Cost Recovery 
Agreement required by this LLIP Section 5.3 is entered into pursuant to the TO 
Tariff. 
 
 
5.4 
Commencement of Interconnection Activities 
If Large Load Interconnection Customer executes the final Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement, Participating TO and Large Load Interconnection 
Customer shall perform their respective obligations in accordance with the terms 
of the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, subject to modification by FERC.  
Upon submission of an unexecuted Large Load Interconnection Agreement, Large 
Load Interconnection Customer and Participating TO shall promptly comply with 
the unexecuted Large Load Interconnection Agreement, if agreed to by the Parties 
pursuant to LLIP Section 5.3, subject to modification by FERC. 
 
Section 6. 
Construction of Participating TO's Interconnection Facilities and Large 
Load Network Upgrades  
 
 
6.1 
Schedule 
Participating TO and Large Load Interconnection Customer shall negotiate in 
good faith concerning a schedule for the Participating TO’s construction of 
Participating TO's Interconnection Facilities and the Large Load Network 
Upgrades.  
 
 
6.2 
Construction Sequencing 
 
6.2.1 General.  In general, the Service Commencement Date will determine the 
sequence of construction of Large Load Network Upgrades. 
 
6.2.2 Advancing Construction of Large Load Network Upgrades that are 
Part of an Expansion Plan of the Participating TO.  A Large Load 
Interconnection Customer with a Large Load Interconnection Agreement,

28 
 
in order to maintain its Service Commencement Date, may request that 
Participating TO advance to the extent necessary the completion of Large 
Load Network Upgrades that:  (i) are necessary to support such Service 
Commencement Date and (ii) would otherwise not be completed, pursuant 
to an expansion plan of Participating TO or approved ISO Transmission 
Plan covering the Participating TO’s facilities, in time to support such 
Service Commencement Date.  Upon such request, Participating TO will 
use Reasonable Efforts to advance the construction of such Large Load 
Network Upgrades to accommodate such request; provided that Large 
Load Interconnection Customer commits to pay Participating TO any 
associated expediting costs.   
 
6.3 
Special Provisions for Affected Systems   
The Large Load Interconnection Customer shall timely enter into and maintain an 
agreement with each applicable Affected System Operator for each addition, 
modification, or upgrade to an Affected System identified through the 
Interconnection Studies or an applicable Affected System study.  The agreement 
shall specify the terms governing payments to be made by the Large Load 
Interconnection Customer to the Affected System Operator, including financial 
security or credit support sufficient to protect the Affected System Operator and 
its other customers against cost shifting.  Where a Cost Recovery Agreement 
applies, the Large Load Interconnection Customer shall provide the Participating 
TO the evidence of such agreements required by, and within the time specified in, 
the Cost Recovery Agreement, and the Participating TO may decline to 
commence, or may suspend, construction as provided in the Cost Recovery 
Agreement.   
 
Section 7. 
Miscellaneous 
 
7.1 
Confidentiality 
 
For the purposes of this LLIP Section 7.1, “Party” or “Parties” shall mean the 
Participating TO, Large Load Interconnection Customer, ISO, or any combination 
of the Participating TO, Large Load Interconnection Customer, or ISO.  
 
Confidential Information shall include, without limitation, all information relating 
to a Party's technology, research and development, business affairs, and pricing. 
 
Information is Confidential Information only if it is clearly designated or marked 
in writing as confidential on the face of the document, or, if the information is 
conveyed orally or by inspection, if the Party providing the information orally 
informs the Party receiving the information that the information is confidential. 
 
If requested by either Party, the other Party shall provide in writing, the basis for 
asserting that the information referred to in this LLIP Section 7.1 warrants 
confidential treatment, and the requesting Party may disclose such writing to the

29 
 
appropriate Governmental Authority.  Each Party shall be responsible for the 
costs associated with affording confidential treatment to its information. 
 
 
 
7.1.1 Scope.  Confidential Information shall not include information that the 
receiving Party can demonstrate: (1) is generally available to the public 
other than as a result of a disclosure by the receiving Party; (2) was in the 
lawful possession of the receiving Party on a non-confidential basis before 
receiving it from the disclosing Party; (3) was supplied to the receiving 
Party without restriction by a third party, who, to the knowledge of the 
receiving Party after due inquiry, was under no obligation to the disclosing 
Party to keep such information confidential; (4) was independently 
developed by the receiving Party without reference to Confidential 
Information of the disclosing Party; (5) is, or becomes, publicly known, 
through no wrongful act or omission of the receiving Party or Breach of 
the Large Load Interconnection Agreement; or (6) is required, in 
accordance with LLIP Section 7.1.6, Order of Disclosure, to be disclosed 
by any Governmental Authority or is otherwise required to be disclosed by 
law or subpoena, or is necessary in any legal proceeding establishing 
rights and obligations under the Large Load Interconnection Agreement. 
Information designated as Confidential Information will no longer be 
deemed confidential if the Party that designated the information as 
confidential notifies the other Party that it no longer is confidential. 
 
7.1.2  Release of Confidential Information.  Neither Party shall release or 
disclose Confidential Information to any other person, except to its 
Affiliates (limited by the Standards of Conduct requirements), employees, 
consultants, Affected System Operators, the Large Load Customer, or to 
parties who may be providing or considering providing financing to or 
equity participation with Large Load Interconnection Customer or the 
Large Load Customer, or to potential purchasers or assignees of Large 
Load Interconnection Customer or the Large Load Customer, on a need-
to-know basis in connection with these procedures, unless such person has 
first been advised of the confidentiality provisions of this LLIP Section 7.1 
and has agreed to comply with such provisions.  Notwithstanding the 
foregoing, a Party providing Confidential Information to any person shall 
remain primarily responsible for any release of Confidential Information 
in contravention of this LLIP Section 7.1. 
 
7.1.3 Rights.  Each Party retains all rights, title, and interest in the Confidential 
Information that each Party discloses to the other Party.  The disclosure by 
each Party to the other Party of Confidential Information shall not be 
deemed a waiver by either Party or any other person or entity of the right 
to protect the Confidential Information from public disclosure. 
 
7.1.4 No Warranties.  By providing Confidential Information, neither Party 
makes any warranties or representations as to its accuracy or 
completeness.  In addition, by supplying Confidential Information, neither

30 
 
Party obligates itself to provide any particular information or Confidential 
Information to the other Party nor to enter into any further agreements or 
proceed with any other relationship or joint venture. 
 
7.1.5 Standard of Care.  Each Party shall use at least the same standard of care 
to protect Confidential Information it receives as it uses to protect its own 
Confidential Information from unauthorized disclosure, publication or 
dissemination.  Each Party may use Confidential Information solely to 
fulfill its obligations to the other Party under these procedures or its 
regulatory requirements. 
 
7.1.6 Order of Disclosure.  If a court or a Governmental Authority or entity 
with the right, power, and apparent authority to do so requests or requires 
either Party, by subpoena, oral deposition, interrogatories, requests for 
production of documents, administrative order, or otherwise, to disclose 
Confidential Information, that Party shall provide the other Party with 
prompt notice of such request(s) or requirement(s) so that the other Party 
may seek an appropriate protective order or waive compliance with the 
terms of these confidentiality provisions. Notwithstanding the absence of a 
protective order or waiver, the Party may disclose such Confidential 
Information which, in the opinion of its counsel, the Party is legally 
compelled to disclose.  Each Party will use Reasonable Efforts to obtain 
reliable assurance that confidential treatment will be accorded any 
Confidential Information so furnished. 
 
7.1.7 Remedies.  The Parties agree that monetary damages would be inadequate 
to compensate a Party for the other Party's Breach of its obligations under 
this LLIP Section 7.1.  Each Party accordingly agrees that the other Party 
shall be entitled to equitable relief, by way of injunction or otherwise, if 
the first Party Breaches or threatens to Breach its obligations under this 
LLIP Section 7.1, which equitable relief shall be granted without bond or 
proof of damages, and the receiving Party shall not plead in defense that 
there would be an adequate remedy at law.  Such remedy shall not be 
deemed an exclusive remedy for the Breach of this LLIP Section 7.1, but 
shall be in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity.  The 
Parties further acknowledge and agree that the covenants contained herein 
are necessary for the protection of legitimate business interests and are 
reasonable in scope.  No Party, however, shall be liable for indirect, 
incidental, or consequential or punitive damages of any nature or kind 
resulting from or arising in connection with this LLIP Section 7.1. 
 
7.1.8 Disclosure to FERC, its Staff, or a State.  Notwithstanding anything in 
this LLIP Section 7.1 to the contrary, and pursuant to 18 CFR section 
1b.20, if FERC or its staff, during the course of an investigation or 
otherwise, requests information from one of the Parties that is otherwise 
required to be maintained in confidence pursuant to the LLIP, the Party 
shall provide the requested information to FERC or its staff, within the

31 
 
time provided for in the request for information.  In providing the 
information to FERC or its staff, the Party must, consistent with 18 CFR 
section 388.112, request that the information be treated as confidential and 
non-public by FERC and its staff and that the information be withheld 
from public disclosure.  Parties are prohibited from notifying the other 
Party prior to the release of the Confidential Information to FERC or its 
staff.  The Party shall notify the other Party to the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement when it is notified by FERC or its staff that a 
request to release Confidential Information has been received by FERC, at 
which time either of the Parties may respond before such information 
would be made public, pursuant to 18 CFR section 388.112.  Requests 
from a state regulatory body conducting a confidential investigation shall 
be treated in a similar manner, consistent with applicable state rules and 
regulations. 
 
7.1.9 Subject to the exception in LLIP Section 7.1.8, any information that a 
Party claims is competitively sensitive, commercial or financial 
information ("Confidential Information") shall not be disclosed by the 
other Party to any person not employed or retained by the other Party, 
except to the extent disclosure is (i) required by law; (ii) reasonably 
deemed by the disclosing Party to be required to be disclosed in 
connection with a dispute between or among the Parties, or the defense of 
litigation or dispute; (iii) otherwise permitted by consent of the other 
Party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld;  or (iv) necessary to 
fulfill its obligations under this LLIP or as a Participating TO, including 
disclosing the Confidential Information to the ISO or to a subregional, 
regional or national reliability organization or planning group.  The Party 
asserting confidentiality shall notify the other Party in writing of the 
information it claims is confidential.  Prior to any disclosures of the other 
Party's Confidential Information under this subparagraph, or if any third 
party or Governmental Authority makes any request or demand for any of 
the information described in this subparagraph, the disclosing Party agrees 
to promptly notify the other Party in writing and agrees to assert 
confidentiality and cooperate with the other Party in seeking to protect the 
Confidential Information from public disclosure by confidentiality 
agreement, protective order or other reasonable measures. 
 
7.1.10 This provision shall not apply to any information that was or is hereafter in 
the public domain (except as a result of a Breach of this provision). 
 
7.1.11 Participating TO shall, at Large Load Interconnection Customer's election, 
destroy, in a confidential manner, or return the Confidential Information 
provided at the time the Confidential Information is no longer needed. 
 
 
7.2 
Disputes

32 
 
 
 
7.2.1  Submission.  In the event either Party has a dispute, or asserts a claim, that 
arises out of or in connection with the Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement, the LLIP, or their performance, such Party (the "disputing

Supplemental MTRC. Beginning on the in-service date of each Covered Upgrade,

6.9. 
Prospective Reassignment of Revenue Responsibility.  
6.9.1. Eligibility for Reassignment of Revenue Responsibility. Whether or not the 
Large Load Customer remains in service, a portion of the prospective revenue 
responsibility associated with a Large Load-Driven Upgrade may be reassigned to a 
subsequent load customer if an objective transmission study conducted under the 
applicable tariff or study process determines that: 
(a) the subsequent large load customer relies upon identifiable incremental 
capability created by the Large Load-Driven Upgrade; and 
(b) that reliance avoids or reduces identifiable transmission upgrades that 
otherwise would have been required to provide the subsequent large load 
customer’s requested service. 
Incidental power flows, generalized system benefits, or use of the transmission 
system that does not satisfy both requirements shall not support a reassignment. 
This Section 6.9 applies only to a load customer other than the Large Load 
Customer, at a facility other than the Large Load Facility. It does not apply to a 
transfer of ownership or operation of the Large Load Facility, a change in Eligible 
Customer, or an assignment of this Agreement, which are governed by Sections 
6.10 and 10.1 and do not alter the Applicable Allocation Percentage or the Large 
Load-Driven Upgrades attributable to the Large Load Facility. 
6.9.2. Reassignment Calculation. LS Power Grid shall determine the prospective 
reassignment separately for each Large Load-Driven Upgrade satisfying Section 
6.9.1 (each, a “Shared Upgrade”). For each Shared Upgrade: 
(a) the Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost shall equal the reasonable 
estimated cost of the transmission upgrades that would have been required 
for the subsequent large load customer absent the Shared Upgrade, less the 
reasonable estimated cost of any additional transmission upgrades required 
when the capability of the Shared Upgrade is considered; 
(b) the Remaining Allocated Net Plant shall equal the portion of the Shared 
Upgrade’s net plant balance included in rate base immediately before the 
reassignment that remains assigned to the Large Load Customer under this 
Agreement; 
(c) the Capability-Supported Amount shall equal the portion of the Remaining 
Allocated Net Plant reasonably attributable to the incremental capability of

29 
 
the Shared Upgrade actually relied upon by the subsequent large load 
customer; and 
(d) the Reassigned Investment Amount shall equal the least of: 
(i) the Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost; 
(ii) the Capability-Supported Amount; and 
(iii) the Remaining Allocated Net Plant. 
The Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost, Capability-Supported Amount, and 
Remaining Allocated Net Plant shall be determined using a consistent cost basis and 
price year. If Remaining Allocated Net Plant is greater than zero, the Reassignment 
Percentage shall equal the Reassigned Investment Amount divided by the 
Remaining Allocated Net Plant, bounded between zero and one hundred percent 
(100%). If Remaining Allocated Net Plant is zero or negative, no Reassignment 
Percentage shall be calculated under this methodology; any reassignment shall 
require an applicable tariff methodology or Commission determination addressing 
that circumstance. 
6.9.3. Prospective Adjustment of Revenue Responsibility. Beginning on the 
Reassignment Effective Date, the applicable Annual MTRC assigned to the Large 
Load Customer shall be prospectively reduced by the Reassignment Percentage 
applied to the Shared Upgrade. LS Power Grid shall record a separate effective 
prospective reassignment credit in the Cumulative Revenue Ledger equal to the 
Reassignment Percentage multiplied by the Remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility associated with the Shared Upgrade that remains assigned to the 
Large Load Customer immediately before the Reassignment Effective Date. That 
credit shall be the sole Cumulative Revenue Ledger adjustment for the reassigned 
responsibility. It shall not adjust the Total Required Revenue Commitment or result 
in a second reduction to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility or 
Required Operational Security for the same reassigned responsibility. 
LS Power Grid shall recalculate the Supplemental MTRC and Operational Security 
under this Agreement to reflect the reassignment. The Reassignment Effective Date 
shall be the latest of: 
(a) the date the subsequent large load customer commences the service for 
which the Shared Upgrade provides the identified incremental capability; 
(b) the effective date of a cost recovery agreement establishing the subsequent 
large load customer’s corresponding revenue responsibility; 
(c) the date on which all Security required from the eligible customer serving 
the subsequent large load customer becomes effective; and 
(d) the date on which the study and any other approvals required under the 
applicable tariff become final. 
No reduction in the Large Load Customer’s Operational Security shall occur until 
the corresponding responsibility and required Security have become effective for the 
subsequent large load customer.

30 
 
6.9.4. Prospective Treatment and Prevention of Duplicate Reassignment. A 
reassignment under this Section shall: 
(a) operate prospectively only and shall not produce a refund, credit, or 
reopening of amounts properly determined for a prior Rate Year; 
(b) transfer prospective revenue responsibility only and shall not constitute a 
sale or transfer of transmission facilities, a transfer of plant ownership, a 
change in plant accounting, or a modification of any CAISO cost allocation; 
(c) not exceed the prospective responsibility remaining under this Agreement 
for the Shared Upgrade; and 
(d) not assign the same transmission capability, avoided upgrade cost, Annual 
MTRC, or Cumulative Revenue Responsibility to more than one large load 
customer. 
LS Power Grid shall maintain an upgrade-specific reassignment ledger identifying 
the capability and responsibility assigned to each large load customer. Once 
responsibility has been effectively reassigned, that responsibility shall not revert to 
the Large Load Customer if the subsequent large load customer later terminates, 
reduces, or fails to commence service. The reassigned responsibility shall instead 
remain with the subsequent large load customer and the Eligible Customer 
responsible for its payment, subject to any further prospective reassignment 
permitted under the applicable agreement and tariff. 
Any prospective reassignment, adjustment, or change in the cost share of a CAISO-
Assigned Regional Project shall be recognized under this Agreement only to the 
extent authorized or required by the CAISO Tariff or a Commission-accepted 
methodology. LS Power Grid shall apply an effective change prospectively to the 
Regional Project Allocated ARR, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, 
Supplemental MTRC, TRBAA Credit, and Operational Security, and shall update 
Schedule 4 and the applicable workpapers. The change shall not assign the same 
project share to more than one customer or alter costs allocated to other customers 
under the CAISO Tariff. 
6.10. Change in Eligible Customer. Cost responsibility is assigned to the Large Load

wholesale transmission service on behalf of the Large Load Customer and Large Load 
Facility. If the Eligible Customer serving a Large Load Customer or Large Load

agreement covering the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and any outstanding

Following the complete departure of the Large Load Customer, the last responsible 
Eligible Customer remains obligated unless responsibility is transferred under an
