7. Security and Payment Obligations 
7.1. 
Construction Security. Before an applicable Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaches its 
Upgrade In-Service Date, Eligible Customer shall maintain Construction Security 
under the relevant agreement sufficient to secure: 
(a) LS Power Grid’s incurred and irrevocably committed engineering, design, 
procurement, permitting, construction, testing, and related costs attributable 
to that upgrade; and 
(b) the Pre-In-Service Termination Costs described in Section 3.3.2, including 
properly accrued AFUDC and applicable cancellation, demobilization, 
equipment removal, disposition, remediation, and restoration costs 
(“Construction Security”).  
Construction Security secures, but does not limit, Eligible Customer’s liability for 
those amounts. Construction Security provided under the relevant Interconnection 
Agreement or an engineering and procurement agreement for the same costs shall 
count toward, and shall not be duplicated by, the Construction Security required under 
this Agreement. Construction Security shall remain in effect for each Large Load-
Driven Upgrade until that upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date and the 
applicable release or conversion conditions in Section 7.2 are satisfied. 
A Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaching its Upgrade In-Service Date shall not result in 
the release of Construction Security attributable to another Large Load-Driven 
Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date. Eligible Customer shall 
replenish Construction Security within ten (10) Business Days after notice of a 
permitted draw and supporting information if additional secured obligations remain 
and the remaining Construction Security is less than the amount required under this 
Section. 
For a CAISO-Assigned Regional Project owned by LS Power Grid, any pre-service 
payment, contribution, or security required from Eligible Customer for its formally 
assigned share shall be provided only as required by the CAISO Tariff, an applicable 
Interconnection Agreement, or another Commission-accepted arrangement, and shall 
be identified in Schedule 4. This Agreement does not independently require pre-
service Construction Security solely because CAISO has assigned a share of a regional 
project to the Large Load Facility. The treatment of costs for a cancelled or abandoned 
regional project shall be governed by Section 6.3.5 and the applicable Commission 
order, CAISO Tariff, and any project-specific abandoned-plant incentive authorized by 
the Commission. For a project owned by another entity, construction and operational 
security shall be provided under the CAISO Tariff or the arrangement required by 
Section 6.3.6 and Schedule 4; it shall not be treated as LS Power Grid Operational

33 
 
Security unless included in LS Power Grid’s Formula Rate and expressly identified as 
LS Power Grid’s share. 
7.2. 
Delivery of Operational Security. No later than thirty (30) Calendar Days before the 
earliest expected Upgrade In-Service Date identified in Schedule 1 or Regional Project 
In-Service Date identified in Schedule 4 for a LS Power Grid-owned CAISO-Assigned 
Regional Project, Eligible Customer shall deliver Operational Security calculated 
under this Article for the Large Load-Driven Upgrades and LS Power Grid-owned 
CAISO-Assigned Regional Project expected to enter service. Operational Security 
must be fully effective before any applicable Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional 
Project In-Service Date.  
If different Large Load-Driven Upgrades or LS Power Grid-owned CAISO-Assigned 
Regional Projects are expected to reach their applicable in-service dates on different 
dates, LS Power Grid shall recalculate the Required Operational Security before each 
subsequent in-service date to include the additional Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility attributable to the upgrade or project share entering service. Eligible 
Customer shall provide any resulting increase no later than fifteen (15) Business Days 
after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if earlier. 
Inclusion of pre-service Construction Work in Progress in rate base shall not constitute 
an Upgrade In-Service Date or independently trigger the Operational Security 
requirement. Construction Security shall remain applicable to each Large Load-Driven 
Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date. 
No Construction Security attributable to a Large Load-Driven Upgrade shall be 
released or converted unless:  
(a) the Required Operational Security attributable to that upgrade is effective; 
(b) that upgrade has reached its Upgrade In-Service Date; and 
(c) LS Power Grid has determined that all Pre-In-Service Termination Costs and 
other construction-related obligations attributable to that upgrade have been 
paid or adequately reserved for. 
Any portion of Construction Security retained for unresolved construction costs shall 
be released after LS Power Grid determines that those costs have been paid or 
adequately reserved for or, if Section 3.3.2 applies, after the Termination Cost 
Reconciliation becomes final. Failure to timely deliver Required Operational Security 
is a default permitting LS Power Grid, to the extent authorized by the applicable tariffs 
and agreements, to suspend energization or service, terminate applicable 
interconnection arrangements, and draw Construction Security for secured obligations.  
7.3. 
Required Operational Security. Required Operational Security shall equal one 
hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility. LS Power Grid shall reduce that amount only by the portion of 
Qualifying Retail Security Support identified in a currently effective Retail Security 
Certification. A Retail Security Certification is accepted in reliance on Eligible

34 
 
Customer’s representations and does not require LS Power Grid to review the 
underlying retail-security documents in the ordinary course. If LS Power Grid has a 
reasonable basis to question the certification, or after a payment default, Credit 
Review Event, or Material Adverse Credit Event, LS Power Grid may request 
supporting information reasonably necessary to verify continued compliance. Any 
resulting deficiency shall be delivered or restored within fifteen (15) Business Days 
after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if earlier. 
7.4. 
Annual Resizing and Security Notices. LS Power Grid shall recalculate Required 
Operational Security with each Annual Projection, Final MTRC Determination Date, 
recalculation of a Final Annual MTRC under Section 6.3.1, Reconciliation Statement, 
effective prospective reassignment, replacement or expiration of Qualifying Retail 
Security Support, or Credit Review Event. If LS Power Grid reasonably determines 
that the Required Security Amount exceeds available Security, it may issue a Security 
Notice identifying the required increase or restoration and reasonable supporting detail 
then available. Eligible Customer shall provide the required increase or restoration 
within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the Security Notice, or by the 
applicable in-service date if earlier. A reduction shall be released only after the 
relevant calculation and reconciliation are final. 
7.5. 
Form of Operational Security. Except to the extent of currently effective Qualifying 
Retail Security Support, Eligible Customer shall provide direct Operational Security in 
the form of cash, an irrevocable standby Letter of Credit meeting Schedule 3, or any 
combination of cash and Letter of Credit. LS Power Grid may accept another form of 
Security that it determines, in its sole discretion, is acceptable. 
Each Letter of Credit shall have an initial stated term of at least twelve (12) months 
and shall remain continuously effective until released under this Agreement; provided, 
however, that a Letter of Credit may have a stated expiration date before its release 
date if Eligible Customer timely extends or replaces it so that Security in an amount 
not less than the Required Security Amount remains continuously available to LS 
Power Grid.  
If an issuing bank has the right not to renew a Letter of Credit, the Letter of Credit 
shall require the issuing bank to provide LS Power Grid and Eligible Customer at least 
ninety (90) Calendar Days’ prior written notice of nonrenewal. Eligible Customer shall 
provide a conforming extension or replacement Letter of Credit, or additional cash 
collateral or other Security accepted by LS Power Grid, no later than sixty (60) 
Calendar Days before the applicable expiration date.   
If Eligible Customer fails to provide the required extension, replacement, or other 
Security by that deadline, LS Power Grid may, before the Letter of Credit expires, 
draw all or any portion of the then-available amount under the Letter of Credit and 
retain the proceeds as cash collateral, apply the proceeds to secured obligations, or 
both. Any proceeds retained but not applied shall continue to constitute Security until 
released under this Agreement.

35 
 
7.6. 
Draw and Application. LS Power Grid may draw against all or any portion of a 
Letter of Credit, apply cash collateral, or apply another form of Security accepted by 
LS Power Grid to secured obligations upon: (a) an unpaid Supplemental MTRC, true-
up, Termination Fee, or other amount due after the applicable payment period; (b) 
Eligible Customer’s failure to timely deliver, maintain, replace, restore, or increase 
Security; (c) cancellation, termination, withdrawal, abandonment, or permanent 
cessation of the Large Load Facility or a material breach of this Agreement; (d) a 
material inaccuracy in a Retail Security Certification or Security instrument; (e) 
Eligible Customer: (i) files a voluntary petition in bankruptcy or seeks reorganization, 
arrangement, or similar relief under any bankruptcy, insolvency, or debtor-relief law; 
(ii) becomes subject to an involuntary bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding that is not 
dismissed within sixty (60) Calendar Days; (iii) has a receiver, trustee, liquidator, or 
custodian appointed for it or a substantial portion of its assets, which appointment is 
not vacated within sixty (60) Calendar Days; (iv) makes a general assignment for the 
benefit of creditors; or (v) admits in writing its inability to pay debts as they become 
due; or (f) Eligible Customer fails to extend, replace, or otherwise maintain Security in 
the amount and within the time required by Section 7.5, including following a notice 
of nonrenewal, issuer rating reduction, or other event affecting the availability of a 
Letter of Credit. 
A draw shall not automatically require replenishment to the amount maintained 
immediately before the draw. Following any application of drawn proceeds to an 
amount due, LS Power Grid shall recalculate the remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility and the Operational Security then required under this Article. Eligible 
Customer shall replenish only the amount, if any, by which the remaining Operational 
Security is less than the recalculated Required Security Amount, within fifteen (15) 
Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if 
earlier. 
Proceeds drawn solely to prevent the expiration or nonrenewal of a Letter of Credit, 
and cash collateral not yet applied to an identified payment obligation, shall remain 
refundable Security and shall continue to constitute Operational Security until applied 
to an amount then due or released under Section 7.9. Such proceeds and cash collateral 
shall be included in determining the amount of remaining Operational Security and 
shall not create an additional replenishment obligation merely because they are held by 
LS Power Grid. 
The posting, drawing, holding, replacement, or replenishment of Operational Security 
shall not, by itself, satisfy the secured obligation, reduce Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility, or produce a TRBAA Credit. Drawn proceeds of Operational Security 
shall become Applied Security Proceeds only when LS Power Grid applies them to an 
identified Supplemental MTRC, prior-period true-up adjustment, Termination Fee, or 
other secured payment obligation arising under Article 6 or Section 3.3.4. Upon 
application, the proceeds shall reduce that obligation dollar-for-dollar and shall receive 
the TRBAA treatment required by Section 6.8; provided, however, that Applied 
Security Proceeds applied to a Termination Fee shall be administered under Section 
3.3.4 and credited to transmission customer only through the Annual Termination Fee

36 
 
Credits provided under Section 6.8. Proceeds of Construction Security applied to Pre-
In-Service Termination Costs or other construction-related obligations shall be treated 
as provided in Sections 3.3.2 and 3.3.3. 
7.7. 
Security Maintenance. Because Required Operational Security is initially one 
hundred percent (100%) of nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, 
no separate acceleration concept applies. An incorrect, expired, withdrawn, 
unavailable, or materially misleading Retail Security Certification, or the loss of

uncovered amount within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice,

Post-Termination Administration and Cash Collateral. LS Power Grid shall

Responsibility and all other obligations under this Agreement have been finally

that cash collateral and proceeds of Security be treated as a deposit or deferred liability 
rather than as a Contribution in Aid of Construction, customer financing of 
transmission plant, or a reduction to LS Power Grid’s rate base. To the extent 
permitted by applicable Commission accounting and ratemaking requirements and tax 
law, LS Power Grid shall record and administer such amounts as the corresponding 
annual costs and payment obligations arise. The treatment described in this Section is 
subject to the Commission’s Uniform System of Accounts, the Formula Rate, the 
Protocols, applicable Commission orders, and other Applicable Laws and Regulations. 
If the Commission requires a different accounting or ratemaking treatment, LS Power 
Grid shall implement the required treatment and make corresponding adjustments 
necessary to prevent duplicate recovery and preserve, to the extent permitted, the 
economic allocation established by this Agreement. The Parties shall cooperate in 
seeking any necessary Commission authorization or acceptance.  
Nothing in this Agreement guarantees a particular accounting, ratemaking, or tax 
result. Cash collateral and unapplied Security proceeds shall remain subject to release 
under Section 7.9, including release to reflect an effective prospective reassignment 
under Section 6.9. 
7.9. 
Release of Security. LS Power Grid shall release excess Operational Security only 
after the applicable Reconciliation Statement becomes final. LS Power Grid shall 
release Security attributable to an effective prospective reassignment and shall release

7.10. Security Does Not Limit Liability. The Required Security Amount is based on LS 
Power Grid’s then-current estimates and calculations and does not cap, replace, or

37 
 
discharge Eligible Customer’s underlying obligations. A shortfall between Security

termination after an Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional Project In-Service Date

If a Party is rendered unable, wholly or in part, by Force Majeure to carry out a

11. Disputes 
All disputes, claims, or controversies arising out of or relating to this Agreement, including 
any dispute concerning the identification or allocation of Large Load-Driven Upgrades or 
Covered Upgrades; any calculation, update, or recalculation of an Estimated Annual MTRC, 
Final Annual MTRC, Regional Project Allocated ARR, or the MTRC Calculation Template; 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues; Supplemental MTRC; Total Required Revenue 
Commitment; Cumulative Revenue Responsibility; TRBAA Credits; Pre-In-Service 
Termination Costs; the Termination Fee; prospective reassignment; or Security, shall be 
resolved under this Article 11, except that a dispute concerning CAISO’s designation of a 
regional project or assignment of a project cost share shall be resolved under the applicable 
CAISO Tariff procedures. Any payment, refund, credit, or other adjustment resulting from the 
resolution of a dispute under this Article 11 shall be implemented as provided in Section 11.5. 
11.1. Submission and Informal Resolution. In the event of a dispute or claim arising out 
of or relating to this Agreement, the disputing Party shall provide the other Party with 
a written notice describing the dispute (“Notice of Dispute”). The dispute shall be 
referred promptly to designated senior representatives for informal resolution. The 
representatives shall meet or confer within ten (10) Business Days and shall use 
reasonable efforts to resolve the matter within thirty (30) Calendar Days after receipt 
of the Notice of Dispute. This informal process is not a condition to seeking 
emergency relief, filing a FERC complaint, or invoking any ADR processes. 
11.2. Alternative Dispute Resolution. If a dispute is not resolved informally, any Party 
may request Alternative Dispute Resolution (“ADR”). The Parties shall use the ADR 
procedures, neutral-selection process, confidentiality protections, and timing 
requirements specified in the applicable FERC rules. ADR shall be conducted by 
persons knowledgeable in electric utility, transmission, and FERC matters and shall 
not alter a jurisdictional rate, term, or condition unless accepted or approved by the 
FERC.

40 
 
11.3. FERC Complaints and Other Rights. Any Party may instead file a complaint, 
petition, or other pleading with the FERC under Section 206 or Section 306 of the 
Federal Power Act, or seek other relief available under the Federal Power Act or 
Applicable Laws and Regulations, and LS Power Grid may make any filing under 
Section 205 of the Federal Power Act permitted by Section 12.12. No Party’s 
participation in informal negotiations or ADR waives or limits its right to seek FERC 
action. A final ADR determination affecting jurisdictional rates, terms, conditions, 
charges, or Network Upgrades shall be filed with the FERC if required. 
11.4. Costs and Interim Performance. Unless otherwise determined through ADR, the 
Parties shall bear their own costs and share neutral costs as specified by the applicable 
ADR procedure. During a dispute, each Party shall continue performing undisputed 
payment and operational obligations, and shall pay undisputed amounts when due.  
11.5. Implementation of Dispute Determinations; TRBAA. Within thirty (30) Calendar 
Days after a dispute under this Article 11 is finally resolved, whether by written 
agreement of the Parties, a final ADR determination (subject to any required 
Commission filing or acceptance), or a final Commission order (each, a “Dispute 
Determination”), LS Power Grid shall: (a) update the affected MTRC Calculation 
Template, Schedules, Cumulative Revenue Ledger, Reconciliation Statement, and 
Required Operational Security, as applicable, and serve the updated documents on 
Eligible Customer; and (b) invoice or refund, as applicable, any amount owed between 
the Parties as a result of the Dispute Determination, without interest. To the extent a 
Dispute Determination changes a TRBAA Credit or any other amount previously 
credited to, or recovered from, transmission customers, including any change in 
Supplemental MTRC Receipts or Applied Security Proceeds for a prior Rate Year, LS 
Power Grid shall record the resulting difference in the TRBA under Section 6.8 and 
flow it through to transmission customers through the TRBAA, and any amount so 
returned by LS Power Grid to transmission customers shall include interest as 
provided in Section 5.3 of the TO Tariff. If a final Commission order in a proceeding 
concerning LS Power Grid’s TRBAA requires a change to any TRBAA Credit 
attributable to this Agreement, LS Power Grid shall implement that order in the TRBA 
and shall make any corresponding updates and adjustments between the Parties under 
this Section 11.5 as if the order were a Dispute Determination. Nothing in this Section 
reopens the Final Annual MTRC or Total Required Revenue Commitment except as 
required to implement a Dispute Determination or as permitted by Section 6.3.1.

Schedule 2 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues Methodology 
1. Purpose and Controlling Principles 
This Schedule establishes the reproducible methodology for calculating projected and actual 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues attributable to the Large Load Facility. It is intended to 
identify wholesale transmission revenues paid by or on behalf of Eligible Customer that are 
attributable to the Large Load Facility and reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected 
from CAISO customers or directly credit LS Power Grid’s Net Revenue Requirement. Such 
revenues may include applicable TAC revenues and qualifying Wheeling Access Charges or 
other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or transmission-service charges under the 
CAISO Tariff or another Commission-accepted arrangement, including charges paid through a 
non-PTO serving entity. The Supplemental MTRC therefore measures only the remaining 
shortfall below the applicable Annual MTRC. 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall be counted once in calculating the Supplemental MTRC 
and the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility against the combined Annual MTRC for all Covered 
Upgrades. They shall not also be treated as a TRBAA Credit under Section 6.8 because they 
reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers. This Schedule does 
not modify CAISO settlement rules, establish a retail rate, impose any obligation on CAISO, or 
alter any cost allocation established under the CAISO Requirements.

4. Applicable Withdrawals 
For each CAISO settlement interval or other reproducible billing interval, Applicable 
Withdrawals shall equal the metered energy withdrawals attributable to the Large Load Facility 
at the metering point identified in Section 2 of this Schedule, expressed in MWh and adjusted as 
follows: 
(a) Imports, exports, station service, auxiliary load, behind-the-meter generation, storage 
charging and discharging, and other injections or withdrawals shall be treated 
consistently with the manner in which they are recognized for the applicable TAC charge 
under the CAISO Tariff. 
(b) Distribution losses and transmission losses shall be included only to the extent they are 
included in the billing determinant for the applicable TAC component. The loss factor or 
method shall be identified in the project-specific table in Section 10 of this Schedule. 
(c) If the Large Load Facility shares a meter or settlement identifier with other load, the 
withdrawals attributable to the Large Load Facility shall be determined from revenue-
quality submeters or another objective allocation method identified in Section 10 of this 
Schedule. An allocation based solely on estimates may be used temporarily but shall be 
reconciled when reliable data become available. 
(d) Withdrawals shall not be counted for a period before the corresponding Annual MTRC is 
included in the Supplemental MTRC calculation under Section 6.4 of the Agreement, 
except where necessary to correct a prior-period error or resettlement. 
5. Applicable TAC Revenue 
Applicable TAC Revenue for an interval shall equal Applicable Withdrawals multiplied by the 
CAISO transmission rate or rates actually applicable to those withdrawals for that interval. The 
calculation shall include only transmission charge components that contribute to recovery of the 
revenue requirement in which LS Power Grid’s costs are included. It shall exclude retail 
distribution charges, generation charges, non-transmission surcharges, taxes collected for another 
governmental entity, and any other charge that does not contribute to recovery of LS Power 
Grid’s transmission revenue requirement. 
If CAISO uses a monthly, annual, or other non-interval billing determinant, LS Power Grid shall 
perform the calculation using that same billing period and determinant. If more than one TAC 
rate or component applies, each component shall be calculated separately before applying the LS 
Power Grid Allocation Factor. 
6. LS Power Grid Allocation Factor 
The LS Power Grid Allocation Factor shall identify the portion of Applicable TAC Revenue 
allocable to LS Power Grid for the relevant period. Unless a different Commission-accepted 
method is stated in Section 10 of this Schedule, the factor shall be calculated from the same 
revenue requirement, billing determinant, allocation percentage, and other inputs used by CAISO 
to include LS Power Grid’s net transmission revenue requirement in the applicable TAC rate. 
For each applicable rate component and period:

Schedule 2 - 4 
 
LS Power Grid Allocation Factor = LS Power Grid Net Revenue Requirement included in 
the applicable TAC component ÷ Total Net Revenue Requirement recovered through that 
TAC component. 
If LS Power Grid’s revenue requirement is recovered through a project-specific, zonal, or other 
direct allocation rather than a systemwide factor, the corresponding Commission-accepted 
allocation percentage or rate component shall be used. The supporting workpapers shall identify 
the source and calculation of each factor. 
7. Calculation of Qualifying Transmission Revenues 
Projected and actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall be calculated as follows for each 
applicable interval, month, or billing period and then aggregated for the Rate Year or partial Rate 
Year: 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues =  Qualifying TAC Revenue + Qualifying Wheeling and 
Other Wholesale Transmission Revenues ± Applicable Adjustments. 
Qualifying TAC Revenue = Σ [(Applicable Withdrawals × Applicable TAC Rate) × LS Power 
Grid Allocation Factor]. Qualifying Wheeling and Other Wholesale Transmission Revenues 
equal Wheeling Access Charges and other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or

Appendix VI  LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION PROCEDURES

1 
 
 
 
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION PROCEDURES (LLIP) 
 
 
Section 1. 
Objectives and Applicability  
1.1 Objectives 
 
The objective of this LLIP is to implement requirements for Large Load interconnections to the 
Participating TO’s Transmission System pursuant to the TO Tariff.  For purposes of this LLIP, 
the “Participating TO” is LS Power Grid California, LLC (“LS Power Grid”), and the “TO 
Tariff” is the LS Power Grid California, LLC Transmission Owner Tariff.  Because LS Power 
Grid is a Non-Load-Serving Participating TO and has no End-Use Customers, a Large Load 
interconnecting under this LLIP will not be a retail transmission customer of the Participating 
TO.   
 
1.2 Applicability  
 
The LLIP is applicable to a Large Load Interconnection Customer that is either (1) proposing to 
interconnect a Large Load to the Participating TO’s Transmission System; (2) seeking to 
increase the capacity of an existing Large Load processed under the LLIP; or (3) with respect to 
an existing load interconnected to the Participating TO’s Transmission System that was not 
processed under the LLIP, seeking an increase of 50 MW or greater.  This LLIP only applies to 
completed Interconnection Requests submitted after the effective date of this Appendix VI to the 
TO Tariff.  Consistent with Section 10A of the TO Tariff, all requests for ECLL Interconnection 
shall be directed to the Participating TO.  An Interconnection Request submitted under this LLIP 
shall constitute the ECLL Interconnection Application, and the Interconnection Studies and the 
Large Load Interconnection Agreement under this LLIP shall constitute the study process and 
the ECLL Interconnection Agreement, respectively, for purposes of Section 10A of the TO 
Tariff.

Point of Interconnection, pursuant to the terms of the Large Load Interconnection Agreement and
